The compound is the self-sufficient pharmacy. The household becomes a production-diagnosis-administration unit running OODA simultaneously across months of growing season and minutes of acute patient presentation. Medical training alone leaves the operator dependent on external supply; herbalism alone leaves the operator without diagnostic discipline; homestead alone produces without clinical direction. The compound is the plant-to-patient cycle, a closed loop where Nikki Moore's Alkaline Herbal Medicine supplies system-organized protocols, Prepper's Medical Handbook supplies clinical frameworks (SOAP, SAMPLE, MARCH, PAWS, shock staging, fever law, antibiotic selection by syndrome, stepped pain ladder), the Gladstar and Green Herbal Medicine-Maker's Handbook lineage supplies the five preparation methods, and the Storey bulletin library supplies the homestead preservation infrastructure (root cellar, solar pit greenhouse, drying rack). The three sources compose a pharmacy, not a library.

This section installs Interlock B as the self-sufficient pharmacy production loop. You load the nested dual-scale loop architecture (seasonal outer loop · acute inner loop), the shelf-inventory-mapped-to-protocol-library interlock layer where every agent's label cross-references clinical indication, dose, contraindication, expiry, and replacement source, the medical-as-load-bearing rule that without clinical discipline the herbal inventory is a pantry and the homestead output is a grocery list, the 20-to-30 core-agent threshold for pharmacology mastery by indication / contraindication / dose range / preparation method, the three-year maturity horizon for protocol-library stability, the three canonical asymmetric-collapse modes (strong medical + weak herbal → interaction miss · strong herbal + weak medical → diagnosis-wrong pattern · strong medical + herbal + weak homestead → empty shelf), and the install / function / failure / feed-forward handoff. Sources: Moore Alkaline Herbal Medicine (system-organized protocols); Prepper's Medical Handbook (clinical frameworks); Medical Herbalism (pharmacokinetics, dose); Herbal Medicine-Maker's Handbook (five preparations); Storey bulletin library (preservation infrastructure); 01.5–01.8 (trauma, assessment, shock, antibiotic).

04.3.1The nested dual-scale loop architecture

The pharmacy runs two loops at two time scales. Both run continuously. Neither runs alone.

The plant-to-patient cycle
01SEASONAL OUTER LOOP — spring garden and forest harvest plan → grow and wild-harvest → dry, tincture, decoct → store under preservation infrastructure → stock pharmacy with labeled, dated, dose-calibrated preparations. Cadence: annual, with mid-season corrections.
02ACUTE INNER LOOP — presentation → SOAP / SAMPLE intake → differential diagnosis → agent selection matching clinical category to inventory → administration under dose / route / schedule → monitor for adverse effect → log outcome → feed back into next season's harvest plan. Cadence: minutes to hours per episode.

The loops are not independent. The acute inner loop's outcome log is the seasonal outer loop's input data. A household running the compound for three years accumulates a protocol library refined to family presentations, a production capacity sized to household demand, and a personnel skill set across administration and monitoring. THE FEEDBACK CHANNEL IS THE LOG. A pharmacy without adverse-event logging and outcome tracking runs both loops but does not close the compound — the seasonal plan drifts from clinical reality because the feedback never reaches the harvest decision.

04.3.2Installation order — medical first

The medical clinical framework is load-bearing. Without SOAP, SAMPLE, differential diagnosis, and the stepped pain ladder, the herbal inventory is a pantry and the homestead output is a grocery list.

Installation-order failure

Herbalists who install herbal without medical produce agent-correct / diagnosis-wrong treatment: the bacterial pneumonia treated with expectorants because the differential never ruled out bacterial etiology. Homesteaders who install production without clinical direction grow volume without knowing whether the species match household presentation patterns.

Install first the clinical discipline from 01.6, 01.7, and 01.8: MARCH and PAWS for trauma, SAMPLE history for intake, SOAP for assessment, shock staging, fever law, antibiotic selection by syndrome, stepped pain ladder. Install second the herbal pharmacology: Medical Herbalism's science-based dose and pharmacokinetics layer and Moore's system-organized protocols, until the operator knows indication, contraindication, dose range, and preparation method for 20 to 30 common agents. Install third the homestead production infrastructure: greenhouse, root cellar, drying rack, tincture setup, wild-harvest protocol, all sized to household demand. The interlock layer is the shelf-inventory-mapped-to-the-protocol-library. Every agent on the shelf carries its clinical indication, dose range, contraindication, expiry date, and replacement source on the label; the inventory document cross-references diagnostic categories to production capacity, and the family member under acute presentation routes agent-selection from diagnosis to shelf in under 10 minutes.

04.3.3The 20-to-30 core-agent pharmacology threshold

Mastery is measured by the count of agents the operator knows across four axes simultaneously: indication, contraindication, dose range, preparation method.

Core-agent mastery criterion

Per agent, the operator cites from memory: the clinical indication (what it treats), the contraindication (who it harms or what it interacts with), the dose range (by weight and preparation), the preparation method (which of the five: infusion, decoction, tincture, poultice, salve).

Below 20 agents, the pharmacy does not cover common household presentations. Above 30 agents, the operator's working memory degrades under stress and substitution errors rise. The 20 to 30 band is empirical — it matches the top-ten recitable tier plus the twenty supporting tier that most three-year-old household pharmacies stabilize at. The five preparations run orthogonally: the same plant can appear as infusion for acute upper-respiratory, tincture for chronic systemic, poultice for topical, salve for skin integrity, decoction for root-and-bark extraction. THE SAME PLANT IS NOT THE SAME AGENT. Preparation method changes pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, and clinical indication; the operator who conflates them mis-doses across the switch.

04.3.4Calibration thresholds

Interlock B calibration

CORE AGENTS · ≥ 20 stocked and in-date TOP-TEN AGENTS · recitable with dose and contraindication from memory AGENT-TO-ADMINISTRATION · < 10 min for common presentations ANNUAL PRODUCTION · 80–120% of household consumption ADVERSE EVENT RATE · < 2 per 100 administrations GARDEN PLAN · updated annually to reflect prior-year clinical use patterns OUTCOME LOG · maintained per episode; seasonal review cycle

The compound reads ACTIVE when the operator walks to the pantry, selects the correct agent, doses it by weight and preparation, and cites expected time-course under 10 minutes — and when the garden plan this year reflects the clinical patterns of last year. It degrades when agents expire on the shelf unrotated, when the garden plan grows the same species year over year regardless of use, or when the household defers to external urgent care for conditions the pharmacy could handle.

04.3.5Three canonical asymmetric-collapse modes

Asymmetric skill collapse in Interlock B produces three failure patterns, each with a diagnostic signature.

Asymmetric-collapse failure modes
01STRONG MEDICAL + WEAK HERBAL — dispenses the wrong agent or misses an interaction. Case: St. John's Wort recommendation against an undisclosed SSRI regimen.
02STRONG HERBAL + WEAK MEDICAL — treats agent-correct, diagnosis-wrong pattern. Case: bacterial pneumonia treated with expectorants because the differential never ruled out bacterial etiology.
03STRONG MEDICAL + HERBAL + WEAK HOMESTEAD — the library runs and the shelf is empty at the moment of need.

Each failure's counter is a specific audit. For (01), the operator adds an interaction-screen step between diagnosis and agent selection, running the agent's contraindication list against household medication inventory before dispensing. For (02), the operator holds differential-diagnosis rigor ahead of agent pattern-match, and declines to dispense when differential is not closed. For (03), the operator audits shelf quantity against annual consumption monthly and schedules production during the harvest window regardless of the current inventory level.

The same plant is not the same agent. Preparation changes pharmacokinetics; dispensing on species name without preparation specification is a stack, not a compound.

04.3.6Install, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALLATION PROTOCOL. Install clinical framework from 01.5–01.8 (MARCH, PAWS, SAMPLE, SOAP, shock staging, fever law, antibiotic syndrome selection, stepped pain ladder) to threshold. Install herbal pharmacology (20 to 30 core agents at four-axis mastery) on top. Install homestead production infrastructure (greenhouse, root cellar, drying rack, tincture setup, wild-harvest protocol) sized to household demand. Install the shelf-inventory-mapped-to-protocol-library interlock layer with per-agent labeling and cross-referenced inventory document. Run the seasonal loop through one full year-to-year cycle before declaring the compound installed.

FUNCTION IN OPERATION. Acute presentation triggers the inner loop: SOAP / SAMPLE intake, differential diagnosis, agent selection by clinical category and preparation method, administration under dose / route / schedule, adverse-effect monitoring, outcome log. Outcome log feeds the seasonal outer loop's next-year harvest plan, producing a protocol library refined to the family's presentation patterns over 3 years. Agent-to-administration runs under 10 minutes for common presentations. Annual production holds at 80–120% of household consumption.

FAILURE INDICATORS. Agents expire on the shelf unrotated — consumption-production feedback has broken. Garden plan repeats year-over-year regardless of clinical use — the seasonal loop is not consuming the inner loop's output. Household defers to external urgent care for conditions inside the pharmacy's coverage — compound state has dropped below DORMANT. Adverse event rate climbs above 2 per 100 — agent-selection or dose-calibration discipline has drifted. Outcome log lapses — the compound is running as a stack and the operator does not know it.

FEED-FORWARD. Interlock B feeds into Sub-module 05 SUSTAINMENT, where homestead infrastructure expansion (preservation, seed-saving, perennial production) scales the seasonal outer loop against multi-year horizons. It feeds into Sub-module 06 COMMAND through household medical command structure (who assesses, who administers, who logs). It feeds into Sub-module 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT through physiological condition classes that determine when pharmacy output is deployable versus when external supply routes are required. The compound is the information-warfare OODA — Boyd's decision loop scaled from fighter-pilot cockpit to small-cell organizational information system. Comms alone gives you a radio; intel alone gives you an assessment; strategy alone gives you a plan. The compound integrates all three into a running loop where observed signal generates intelligence, intelligence refines strategy, strategy directs communications, communications shape the information environment, and the shaped environment produces new signal. The Area Intelligence Handbook supplies the five-phase intelligence cycle and the Six Layers of the Operational Environment. F3EAD supplies the nested targeting cycle. Sun Tzu anchors know-enemy-know-self at the observation layer; Clausewitz gates the decision layer through friction and the culminating point; the 4GW Handbook identifies the moral level as decisive; Napoleon supplies center-of-gravity targeting; CIA PSYOP doctrine supplies target audience analysis. This section installs Interlock C as the information-warfare OODA. You load the five-phase intelligence cycle (plan · collect · process · analyze · disseminate) with F3EAD (find · fix · finish · exploit · analyze · disseminate) nested inside as the targeting cycle, the Six Layers of the Operational Environment as the orientation frame, the 4GW three-level analysis (physical · mental · moral) that identifies where leverage applies, the intel-as-load-bearing rule that area study is the structural memory on which comms and strategy both plot, the PACE-plan comms architecture (primary · alternate · contingency · emergency) rehearsed monthly on primary-plus-alt and quarterly on all four, the CCIR-tagged traffic discipline that carries relevance / source / audience tags on every transmission, and the install / function / failure / feed-forward handoff. Sources: Boyd (OODA recursion); Area Intelligence Handbook (5-phase cycle, Six Layers, source-reliability grading); F3EAD targeting doctrine; Sun Tzu (observation); Clausewitz (friction, culminating point); 4GW Handbook (three-level analysis); Napoleon (center of gravity); CIA PSYOP (target audience); Baofeng Manual / Frequencies of Survival (radio stack); PACE doctrine; 00.4, 00.6, 00.8, 00.9 (intelligence and OODA base).

04.4.1The five-phase intelligence cycle and F3EAD

The loop runs in a fixed outer-inner architecture. The outer loop is the intelligence cycle. The inner loop is the targeting cycle.

The two nested cycles
01OUTER — FIVE-PHASE INTELLIGENCE CYCLEPlanning & Direction → Collection → Processing → Analysis & Production → Dissemination. Cadence: days to weeks.
02INNER — F3EADFind → Fix → Finish → Exploit → Analyze → Disseminate. Cadence: hours to days.

F3EAD nests inside phase 4 / 5 of the outer cycle — Analysis & Production drives Find, Dissemination drives Fix, and the Exploit-Analyze-Disseminate tail of F3EAD feeds back into the outer cycle's Collection phase. The cell running both cycles simultaneously produces organizational tempo measured in hours rather than the days a cell running only the outer cycle produces. TEMPO IS THE WEAPON. The compound's superiority is not produced by more information — it is produced by faster cycles through the same information, which compounds orientation quality across iterations faster than the adversary's cycle can update.

04.4.2The Six Layers of the Operational Environment

Orientation is not raw signal. It is signal plotted against a structured frame. The Six Layers are that frame.

The Six Layers of the OE

01 · PHYSICAL TERRAIN — ground, built environment, hydrography, vegetation. 02 · INFRASTRUCTURE — power, water, comms, transport, logistics networks. 03 · DEMOGRAPHIC — populations, identities, affiliations, movement patterns. 04 · ECONOMIC — production, distribution, finance, dependencies. 05 · POLITICAL — authority structures, factions, alliances, governance. 06 · INFORMATION — media, narratives, attention flows, perception.

Every operator produces the running six-layer estimate on demand. The estimate is a living document refreshed on cadence (≤ 14 days), not a one-time product. The layers interact — a change in the information layer (a viral narrative) propagates to the political layer, which propagates to the economic layer, which propagates back to the demographic layer. The area study discipline reads these cross-layer propagations as the primary orientation signal. LAYERS COMPOSE. A cell that reads only the physical layer fights yesterday's war; a cell that reads all six reads tomorrow's.

04.4.3Installation order — intelligence first

Intelligence is load-bearing, specifically the Area Study discipline. Area study turns observation into oriented intelligence and gives strategy a target.

Installation-order failure

Comms-first cells run active radio nets with low-value content; operators stay in touch without knowing more. Strategy-first cells build plans against unverified orientation and run at the adversary's tempo. The compound requires intel-first because the orient layer is the compound's load-bearing column.

Install first the intelligence base: AO / AI / NAI bounding, Six-Layer mapping, 5-phase cycle, F3EAD, source-reliability grading (A–F reliability × 1–6 accuracy). Install second the comms base: Baofeng Manual and Frequencies of Survival for the radio stack, PACE-plan rehearsal (primary / alternate / contingency / emergency), net-control discipline, authentication procedure, emissions discipline across transmit windows / low-power modes / geographic separation from base. Install third the strategy base: Sun Tzu for knowing, Clausewitz for friction and culminating point, 4GW for three-level analysis, Napoleon for center-of-gravity targeting. The interlock layer is the intelligence cycle executed over the radio net under progressively higher tempo and progressively worse comms conditions; observation reports from fielded elements come in over comms, process through the orientation frame, produce a decision, and generate outbound traffic directing next-period collection and action.

04.4.4The 4GW three-level analysis

Fourth-Generation Warfare identifies three levels where leverage applies. The moral level is decisive.

The 4GW three levels
01PHYSICAL — force-on-force, material attrition, terrain control. Where conventional militaries fight.
02MENTAL — tempo, surprise, deception, cognitive overload. Where maneuver doctrine operates.
03MORAL — legitimacy, cohesion, the adversary's will to continue. In 4GW, this level is decisive.

A cell that dominates physically while losing morally loses the campaign. The moral level is where narrative warfare operates, where the population's perception of legitimacy is contested, and where the 4GW adversary invests disproportionate effort. The compound's strategic layer reads for moral-level leverage first, mental-level leverage second, physical-level leverage third. TARGET SELECTION RUNS UP THE LEVELS, EXECUTION RUNS DOWN THEM. The commander identifies the decisive level (usually moral), then mental, then the physical action that expresses both.

04.4.5Calibration thresholds

Interlock C calibration

AREA STUDY REFRESH CADENCE · ≤ 14 days PACE PLAN EXERCISE · monthly primary + alternate · quarterly all four SIX-LAYER ESTIMATE · producible on demand by every operator LOOP TEMPO · ≤ 0.5× adversary estimated cycle CCIR-TAGGED TRAFFIC · > 80% of transmissions TARGET AUDIENCE ANALYSIS · documented per major narrative SOURCE-RELIABILITY GRADING · every intel input tagged A-F × 1-6

The compound reads ACTIVE when any operator produces the running six-layer estimate on demand, comms traffic carries CCIR relevance / source evaluation / audience tag on every transmission, strategic posture tracks through DECIDE to observed reality, and loop tempo outpaces the adversary by measurable factor. It degrades when area study lags past 30 days, comms traffic devolves to free-form chatter, decisions bypass orient onto gut, or tempo equalizes with the adversary.

04.4.6Three canonical asymmetric-collapse modes

Asymmetric-collapse failure modes
01STRONG COMMS + WEAK INTEL — active net, low-value content. Operators stay in touch without knowing more.
02STRONG INTEL + WEAK COMMS — individual competence, zero organizational tempo. Intelligence exists and does not propagate.
03STRONG INTEL + COMMS + WEAK STRATEGY — hyperactive reaction loops. High tempo, high drift, no culminating-point discipline.

Adversary targeting attacks the compound's integration through four mechanisms. Deception injection feeds false signal to the orient layer when source-reliability grading is thin. Communications interdiction jams or imitates the comms stack against an unexercised PACE plan. Narrative warfare attacks the population's perception at the 4GW moral level while the cell fights on the physical plane. Tempo disruption forces the cell to react faster than orient can update. Each counter runs at the integration layer: source-reliability grading discipline, PACE rehearsal cadence, moral-level target awareness, orient-layer tempo protection.

04.4.7Install, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALLATION PROTOCOL. Install intelligence base (AO / AI / NAI bounding, Six-Layer mapping, 5-phase cycle, F3EAD, source-reliability grading) to threshold. Install comms base (radio stack, PACE plan, net-control, authentication, emissions discipline) on top. Install strategy base (Sun Tzu, Clausewitz, 4GW, Napoleon) on top. Drill the intelligence-cycle-over-radio-net interlock layer at progressively higher tempo and worse conditions until the cell's loop tempo holds at half the adversary's cycle.

FUNCTION IN OPERATION. Observation reports come in from fielded elements over comms, carrying source-reliability tags. The cell processes them through Six-Layer orientation, runs them through the 5-phase cycle or F3EAD as appropriate, produces decisions tagged with CCIR relevance and target audience, and generates outbound traffic directing next-period collection and action. Area study refreshes on 14 day cadence. Six-Layer estimate holds current on demand. Loop tempo runs at half the adversary's cycle or faster.

FAILURE INDICATORS. Area study lags past 30 days — the orientation frame is stale. CCIR-tagged traffic drops below 80% — transmissions have devolved to free-form chatter. PACE exercise skipped two monthly cycles — the alternate channels have not been validated under stress. Tempo equalizes with the adversary — the compound has lost OODA superiority. Decisions bypass orient onto gut — the cell is running a stack while calling it a compound.

FEED-FORWARD. Interlock C feeds into Sub-module 05 SUSTAINMENT through shared comms infrastructure (repeater networks, long-term antenna systems, spectrum discipline). It feeds into Sub-module 06 COMMAND through the full strategy and leadership doctrine where the information-warfare OODA becomes the commander's orientation instrument. It feeds into Sub-module 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT through command and information condition classes. COMSEC and cyber-OPSEC carry over to VOLUME_002 as explicit expansion targets. INTERLOCK D — Force + Leadership + Strategy (command under fire)

The compound is Command Under Fire — the capacity to decide, direct, and execute under the conditions Clausewitz called friction, the aggregate of everything that degrades plan-to-reality fidelity once contact begins. Force discipline alone produces an operator who executes a directed task; leadership alone produces someone who plans and directs; strategy alone produces someone who reasons about ends and means. The compound is the commander who runs Prioritize-and-Execute inside the force continuum they trained in, against a Clausewitzian friction budget they have modeled, issuing Decentralized Command directives that produce coherent emergent team behavior while the original plan decays by the minute. Willink and Babin's Extreme Ownership supplies the twelve laws; Clausewitz supplies friction / fog / culminating point / center of gravity; Sun Tzu anchors know-enemy-know-self; the 4GW Handbook supplies the three-level target-selection frame; Hopkins's Small Unit Infantry Ambush Tactics supplies the sixty-second-rule under near-ambush compression; Miller's Golden Rule of Combat supplies the "be there with more force at the decisive point" principle; Napoleon supplies the concentration doctrine at small-unit scale.

This section installs Interlock D as the command-under-fire loop. You load the six-beat command cycle (plan → contact → prioritize → execute → absorb → observe) running at 10–60 second cadence under contact, the twelve laws of Extreme Ownership as the leadership substrate, the friction-as-signal reframe where each loop iteration updates the enemy model, team-capability model, and culminating-point estimate, the Decentralized Command architecture where subordinate leaders make local decisions inside commander's intent, the commander-absorbs-friction rule where friction halts at the commander and a recalibrated directive flows downward rather than propagated alarm, the leadership-as-load-bearing rule that without leadership discipline force and strategy are individually competent and do not produce team behavior, the urgency-vs-leverage distinction (P&E Chapter 7 — the loop fails when urgency displaces leverage), and the install / function / failure / feed-forward handoff. Sources: Willink / Babin Extreme Ownership (12 laws, P&E, Decentralized Command, Cover-and-Move); Clausewitz (friction, culminating point, center of gravity, trinity); Sun Tzu (observation); 4GW Handbook (three-level analysis); Hopkins (sixty-second rule, near-ambush); Miller (Golden Rule of Combat); Napoleon (concentration at decisive point); 00.7 and 00.8 (self-assessment, OODA); 03.1–03.11 (full force base).

04.5.1The six-beat command cycle

The loop runs at contact tempo. Each beat feeds the next. The compound turns friction into signal.

The command-under-fire cycle
01PLANPre-contact: strategic intent, order of operations, force-discipline baseline, modeled friction budget.
02CONTACTAdversary acts. Plan begins degrading. Friction rises. The operator observes the delta between plan and reality.
03PRIORITIZEIdentify the highest-leverage next action, not the most urgent. P&E Chapter 7 discipline.
04EXECUTEDirect, not perform. Subordinate leaders operate inside commander's intent under Decentralized Command.
05ABSORBFriction halts at the commander. A recalibrated directive flows downward; alarm does not.
06OBSERVEDid the last directive achieve its purpose? Re-enter beat 03 if not.

Under contact the loop cycles at 10 to 60 second cadence. Under Hopkins's near-ambush conditions the full loop compresses into a single sub-60 second window. The compound's work is done between iterations — each cycle updates the model of what the enemy is doing, what the team is capable of, and where the culminating point sits. A non-compound commander experiences friction as noise. The compound commander experiences friction as signal.

04.5.2The twelve laws of Extreme Ownership

Leadership is load-bearing. Willink and Babin's twelve laws are the twelve-point spine.

The twelve laws

01 · EXTREME OWNERSHIP — the leader owns every outcome in the sphere of command. 02 · NO BAD TEAMS, ONLY BAD LEADERS — team performance reflects leadership. 03 · BELIEVE — the leader must believe in the mission to transmit belief. 04 · CHECK THE EGO — ego compromises assessment. 05 · COVER AND MOVE — no element acts alone. 06 · SIMPLE — complex plans fail to contact; simple plans survive friction. 07 · PRIORITIZE AND EXECUTE — highest-leverage action, not most urgent. 08 · DECENTRALIZED COMMAND — subordinate leaders decide inside intent. 09 · PLAN — the plan is a baseline, not a script; planning discipline survives plan loss. 10 · LEADING UP AND DOWN THE CHAIN — information flows both directions under discipline. 11 · DECISIVENESS AMID UNCERTAINTY — the leader decides with incomplete information. 12 · DISCIPLINE EQUALS FREEDOM — rehearsed discipline is the source of operational flexibility.

The twelve laws install before force rehearsal produces compound behavior. A team whose commander holds the twelve laws at practice intensity translates tempo under contact. A team whose commander holds only the force base produces individually competent operators executing degraded plans. THE 12 LAWS ARE A FOUNDATION, NOT A MENU. Selective adoption — Cover-and-Move without Extreme Ownership, Decentralized Command without Simple — produces internal contradictions the team resolves under stress by defaulting to the strongest operator and collapsing to a stack.

04.5.3The urgency-versus-leverage distinction

P&E Chapter 7 makes the distinction explicit. Under contact, urgency and leverage diverge.

The most urgent action is the one making the loudest noise. The highest-leverage action is the one whose outcome changes the rest of the engagement. The loop fails when urgency displaces leverage.

An enemy casualty calling for medical support is urgent. A flanking element moving on a covered position is high-leverage. A radio traffic jam is urgent. A subordinate leader's request for authorization to seize decisive terrain is high-leverage. The compound commander holds the distinction through the stress of contact. The stack commander responds to urgency and loses leverage. The discipline is trained — it does not install from reading the book alone. It installs through rehearsal where urgent and high-leverage diverge and the commander practices choosing leverage.

04.5.4Installation order — leadership first

Install first the force base — the full Sub-module 03 stack — because commander credibility requires demonstrated competence across what is being directed. Install second the leadership base — the twelve laws internalized and practiced in low-stakes settings where the commander can afford mistakes. Install third the strategy base — the Clausewitz / Sun Tzu / Lind / Napoleon reading integrated into operational vocabulary, not cited as academic reference.

Installation-order failure

Force-first-leadership-later produces competent operators who cannot command. Leadership-first-force-later produces commanders the team does not respect under contact. Strategy-first produces plans without the capacity to execute them. The compound requires all three at threshold and the leadership substrate running under them all.

The interlock layer is team rehearsal under imposed friction: force-on-force exercises where communication degrades mid-exercise, casualties simulate mid-movement, plans change under contact, subordinate leaders drop out mid-engagement; the compound's measurement is team coherence across the injections, not individual performance within them.

04.5.5Calibration thresholds

Interlock D calibration

TEAM TEMPO UNDER CONTACT · ≥ 80% of practice tempo DIRECTIVE-TO-EXECUTION LATENCY · < 15 s SUBORDINATE LEADER INTENT DECISIONS · ≥ 3 per engagement AFTER-ACTION DEBRIEF COMPLETION · 100% COMMANDER-CITABLE CURRENT CENTER OF GRAVITY · YES / NO CULMINATING POINT MODELED PRE-CONTACT · YES / NO

The compound reads ACTIVE when team tempo holds at practice cadence under contact, directives are clear and brief and leave discretion on execution detail, debriefs surface mistakes routinely rather than burying them, and team members show initiative during ambiguous moments. It degrades when orders become more detailed (micromanagement, a sign the commander has lost trust or is overloading the loop), when orders become less frequent (the commander locked in Observe), when subordinates stop making local decisions, or when the culminating point passes unrecognized and the team continues expending resources past value.

04.5.6Adversary targeting of the command compound

A sophisticated adversary targets the compound's integration through four patterns.

Four integration-layer attacks on Interlock D
01DECAPITATIONTarget the commander directly. Counter: Decentralized Command means subordinate leaders continue; organizational resilience is the counter.
02TEMPO DISRUPTIONInject friction to overload the commander's loop. Counter: P&E discipline identifies highest-leverage action and ignores distractor traffic.
03MORAL-LEVEL ATTACKUndermine team faith in the commander's cause through information warfare. Counter: strategic clarity and rehearsed team identity absorb the attack over months.
04OVEREXTENSION TRAPFeign adversary weakness to draw the team past its culminating point. Counter: Clausewitz's culminating-point discipline halts advance when cost to continue exceeds expected gain.

Each attack is cheaper than attritional attack on force or strategy alone. Counter runs at the integration layer: team resilience architecture, P&E rehearsal under friction, strategic narrative clarity, culminating-point modeling pre-contact.

04.5.7Install, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALLATION PROTOCOL. Install force base (full 03.1 through 03.11 stack) to threshold. Install leadership base (twelve laws internalized, practiced in low-stakes settings) on top. Install strategy base (Clausewitz, Sun Tzu, Lind, Napoleon integrated into operational vocabulary) on top. Run team rehearsal under imposed friction — communication degrades, casualties simulate, plans change, subordinate leaders drop out — until team coherence holds across the injections.

FUNCTION IN OPERATION. Pre-contact sets plan, strategic intent, force-discipline baseline, modeled friction budget. Contact activates; the plan begins degrading. The commander prioritizes on leverage, directs under Decentralized Command, absorbs friction at the commander's level, observes outcome, and re-enters the prioritize beat at 10 to 60 second cadence. Each iteration refines the enemy model, team-capability model, and culminating-point estimate. Friction becomes signal.

FAILURE INDICATORS. Orders become more detailed — the commander has lost trust in subordinate leaders or is overloading the loop. Orders become less frequent — the commander is locked in Observe and the team is operating in a directive vacuum. Subordinates stop making local decisions — Decentralized Command has collapsed. Culminating point passes unrecognized — the team continues expending resources past value. After-action debriefs become perfunctory — the feedback channel that turns engagements into compound adaptation has silted over.

FEED-FORWARD. Interlock D feeds into Sub-module 06 COMMAND, where the full leadership and strategy doctrine composes command into campaign-scale operations. It feeds into Sub-module 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT through command condition classes that select the appropriate command tempo for the mission's operational class. It composes with Interlock C (Information-Warfare OODA) at the commander's orientation layer — the commander's decisions consume Interlock C output as primary input. Section 04.6 installs Interlock E, the operator physical specification.

SECTION 04.6

INTERLOCK E — Fitness + Combatives + Mountaineering (operator physical specification)

ARCHITECTURECONDITIONING LOOP (BIOLOGICAL SUBSTRATE)
DOMAINSFITNESS · COMBATIVES · MOUNTAINEERING
LOAD-BEARINGFITNESS PERIODIZATION (AeT ENGINE)

The compound is the Operator Physical Specification — a body conditioned simultaneously across sustained aerobic capacity with load and altitude, explosive power generation under cognitive load, and the general-purpose fitness substrate that underwrites both. Fitness alone produces a gym athlete; combatives alone produces a fighter who gasses under load; mountaineering alone produces an alpinist who cannot generate a hip-drive Dempsey punch at hour eleven. The compound is the operator's body as substrate for every other compound in 04 — the other interlocks assume a body capable of sustaining the loop. House and Johnston's Training for the Uphill Athlete anchors the AeT / LT physiology and polarized distribution; Training for the New Alpinism adds the five periodization principles and TINSTAAFL; Mountaineering: Freedom of the Hills Chapter 4 adds FITT / SMART frames and the baseline fitness test; Dempsey's Championship Fighting supplies the combatives power-generation pathway (falling step, power line, semi-crouch, four methods of weight in motion); Miller's Meditations on Violence Chapter 3 supplies the chemical cocktail and HRmax zones; the "eighty percent of performance is mental" principle closes the loop, because mental fitness is physical.

This section installs Interlock E as the operator's physical specification — the substrate on which every other compound runs. You load the polarized 80/20 distribution across Zone 1–Z2 aerobic volume and Zone 4–Z5 targeted work, the Aerobic Deficiency Syndrome pattern where chronic gray-zone Zone 3 training produces an athlete who cannot go slow and cannot go fast, the five periodization principles + TINSTAAFL that govern multi-year physical development, the Dempsey four methods of weight in motion sustained at HR 170 (the combatives power-generation criterion), the FOTH baseline fitness test (5 mi RT, 13 lb pack, 2000 ft gain, < 2.5 hr), the cross-domain periodization layer where quarterly domain focus rotates while no domain drops below maintenance floor, the five-year continuity horizon that produces a specification unreachable by one year at any intensity, and the install / function / failure / feed-forward handoff. Sources: House / Johnston Training for the Uphill Athlete (AeT / LT, polarized distribution, ADS); Training for the New Alpinism (five principles, TINSTAAFL); Mountaineering: Freedom of the Hills Ch 4 (FITT, SMART, baseline test, Ten Essentials); Dempsey Championship Fighting (four methods, power line, falling step); Miller Meditations on Violence Ch 3 (chemical cocktail, HRmax zones); 01.1 / 01.4 / 01.5 (substrate, energy); 02.9 / 02.10 (mountaineering, fitness base); 03.2 / 03.3 / 03.5 (combatives physiology, decision cycle).

04.6.1The polarized distribution and Aerobic Deficiency Syndrome

Training distribution determines adaptation. The evidence base from alpine and endurance sport is polarized ~80 / 20, not pyramidal.

Training-zone distribution
01POLARIZED~80% Zone 1 and Zone 2 volume (below AeT) + ~20% Zone 4 and Zone 5 targeted work (above LT). Zone 3 intentionally minimized.
02PYRAMIDALVolume pools in Zone 3 (gray zone between AeT and LT). High perceived effort, minimal adaptation. ADS signature.
03ADS PATTERNChronic Zone 3 training produces an athlete who cannot go slow (the body burns glycogen when it should burn fat) and cannot go fast (the LT ceiling does not rise). Diagnostic: nose-breathing at assigned Zone 2 pace fails.

The mechanism is endocrine and metabolic. Zone 1 and Zone 2 training develops the aerobic base — mitochondrial density, capillary density, fat-oxidation capacity. Zone 4 and Zone 5 work raises LT. Zone 3 work produces neither adaptation at high enough stimulus to matter — it only produces fatigue. CHRONIC ZONE 3 IS A TAX, NOT AN INVESTMENT. The operator stuck in gray-zone training feels like they are working hard and measures static across every performance metric; the polarized operator trains in zones that feel either trivial or brutal, and gains in both directions compound.

04.6.2The five periodization principles and TINSTAAFL

Training for the New Alpinism supplies the governing principles for multi-year physical development.

The five principles

01 · CONTINUITY — training effect requires unbroken accumulation; gaps erode the base faster than the work rebuilds it. 02 · GRADUALNESS — volume and intensity increase incrementally; jumps produce injury or regression. 03 · MODULATION — stress cycles with recovery; flat work decays; waves compound. 04 · SPECIFICITY — adaptation matches stimulus; general work has limits the specific work does not. 05 · INDIVIDUALITY — response to stimulus varies; program adapts to the operator, not the reverse.

TINSTAAFL — there is no such thing as a free adaptation. Every gain costs in another domain. The operator peaking strength loses endurance; the operator peaking endurance loses power. The compound's work is to periodize the costs so the losses land on domains currently at floor rather than domains currently load-bearing. THE LAW IS BIOLOGICAL, NOT MOTIVATIONAL. Ignoring TINSTAAFL does not defeat it — it produces untracked costs that surface as injury, overtraining, or asymmetric collapse.

04.6.3Installation order — fitness periodization first

Fitness periodization is load-bearing, specifically the aerobic-threshold base. Without an AeT engine, combatives cannot sustain engagement length and mountaineering caps at short days.

Installation-order failure

Combatives-first athletes gas out of engagement length. Mountaineering-first athletes lack the power to fight. Fitness-first produces the substrate on which combatives power-generation and alpine load-tolerance both install.

Install first 6 to 12 months of Zone 1 and Zone 2 aerobic volume with measured AeT and LT, a training log, a periodized program running continuity / gradualness / modulation. Install second the combatives base — Dempsey's four methods of weight in motion drilled until the falling-step trigger cascade is motor-patterned, the power line wired in, performance-under-cocktail measured through scaled stress drills. Install third the mountaineering base — FOTH's Ten Essentials, the periodized FITT prescription, snow travel, avalanche protocol, glacier rope team, altitude acclimatization. The interlock layer periodizes across all three simultaneously: combatives drills schedule during alpine build phases, alpine volume maintains during combatives peak phases, gym and strength run as the shared substrate; each quarter has a primary domain focus and no domain drops below maintenance floor.

04.6.4The five-year continuity horizon

Continuity compounds year over year. The compound's specification is time-bound, not intensity-bound.

An operator on five years of continuous periodized training produces a physical specification unreachable in one year regardless of intensity.

The mechanism is biological accumulation — capillary density, mitochondrial density, tendon remodeling, bone density, motor-pattern depth — all accrue on time scales the one-year operator cannot shortcut. The operator who skips months and makes them up with high intensity loses the accumulation window without gaining the adaptation. The operator who holds continuity at moderate intensity compounds across years. CONTINUITY BEATS INTENSITY. This inverts the gym-culture default that prescribes higher intensity to compensate for missed sessions; the actual compensation is a return to baseline volume, not a higher-intensity catch-up session.

04.6.5Calibration thresholds

Interlock E calibration

WEEKLY Z1–Z2 VOLUME · 4 to 8 hr minimum POLARIZED DISTRIBUTION · 70–85% Zone 1 and Zone 2 FOTH BASELINE TEST · < 2.5 hr (5 mi RT, 13 lb pack, 2000 ft gain) DEMPSEY FALLING-STEP POWER GENERATION · maintained at HR 170 NOSE-BREATHING ZONE 2 TEST · passing at assigned pace RESTING HR · stable or declining LAST STRENGTH SESSION · within 7 days LAST COMBATIVES DRILL · within 14 days LAST ALPINE OR RUCKED SESSION · within 14 days

The compound reads ACTIVE when all calibrations hold, training log shows consistent monthly volume at polarized distribution, and the operator identifies current periodization phase and what it is building. It degrades when distribution drifts into gray-zone Zone 3 (ADS), when one domain dominates and another erodes (cardio detraining begins at ~14 days of disuse), or when rest days drop and overtraining signatures appear (sleep disruption, resting HR rise, mood shift).

04.6.6Asymmetric collapse and adversary exploitation

Asymmetric-collapse failure modes
01STRONG COMBATIVES + WEAK FITNESS — wins round one and two, loses round three onward. The cocktail survives the sprint and not the sustained engagement.
02STRONG FITNESS + ALPINE + WEAK COMBATIVES — lacks the explosive power and aggression vocabulary for force-continuum Levels 3–6. Endures, does not apply.
03STRONG FITNESS + COMBATIVES + WEAK ALPINE — gym-strong, tactically useless on a multi-day movement. The specification does not deploy.

Adversary exploitation runs three patterns. Tempo asymmetry: a sustained low-intensity adversary outlasts a compound peaked for short bursts; the polarized distribution is the counter. Environmental stressors: altitude unmasks aerobic deficiency, cold unmasks fatigue, load unmasks strength gaps; domain-specific acclimatization is the counter. Medical attrition: injury targets the weakest domain first (the unconditioned knee fails on the long descent, the unconditioned core fails in the grapple); the maintenance-floor rule is the counter.

04.6.7Install, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALLATION PROTOCOL. Install 6 to 12 months Zone 1 / Zone 2 aerobic base with measured AeT / LT and a training log. Install combatives (Dempsey four methods, power line, falling step, semi-crouch, performance-under-cocktail drills) on top. Install mountaineering (FOTH Ten Essentials, FITT prescription, snow / avalanche / glacier / altitude) on top. Periodize across all three with quarterly domain focus and universal maintenance floor. Hold the continuity discipline at minimum five years for the full specification.

FUNCTION IN OPERATION. Weekly Zone 1 / Zone 2 volume holds at 4 to 8 hr at polarized distribution. Dempsey power generation sustains at HR 170. FOTH baseline test clears < 2.5 hr. Nose-breathing Zone 2 passes at assigned pace. Resting HR stable or declining. Strength session within 7 days; combatives and alpine within 14 days. The operator's body operates as substrate for Interlocks A through D simultaneously — detection, production, information, and command loops all run on it.

FAILURE INDICATORS. Distribution drifts into Zone 3 (ADS). Cardio detraining at ~14 days begins. One domain dominates, another erodes below maintenance floor. Rest days drop, overtraining signatures appear (sleep disruption, resting HR rise, mood shift). Training log lapses; the operator trains on feel without feedback. Monthly audit of Interlock E lapses; the decay clock runs silently.

FEED-FORWARD. Interlock E feeds into Sub-module 05 SUSTAINMENT through nutrition and recovery infrastructure (caloric sufficiency, sleep architecture, recovery modalities). It feeds into Sub-module 06 COMMAND through mental resilience substrate — the "eighty percent mental" principle runs on the physical specification. It feeds into Sub-module 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT through physiological condition classes that select acceptable mission envelopes against current physical state. The four prior interlocks compose on top of Interlock E — the substrate is common to all. Section 04.7 installs the compound-recognition layer.

SECTION 04.7

Compound recognition — reading your system for interlock state

FOUR STATESACTIVE · DEGRADING · DORMANT · FAILED
OPERATIONAL CEILING RULEWEAKEST COMPOUND SETS CEILING
AUDIT CADENCEMONTHLY 4-QUESTION · QUARTERLY FULL REVIEW · PRE-MISSION 10-MIN-PER-COMPOUND
SELF-PERCEPTION LAGA: ~30 d · B: ~90 d · C: ~14 d · D: ~60 d · E: 7–14 d
WEAKEST-COMPOUND TRAINING ALLOCATION60–70% WEAKEST · 30–40% OTHERS
INVERTED PYRAMIDSTRONGEST MAINTAINS AT FLOOR · WEAKEST DRIVES INVESTMENT
INTEGRATED PICTURESINGLE-PAGE LIVING DOCUMENT (DESCENDS FROM 00.9 CSP)

Every compound sits in one of four states at any moment: ACTIVE, DEGRADING, DORMANT, or FAILED. The operator's overall readiness is the minimum state across all five compounds, because the weakest compound defines the operational ceiling. The compound audit, run monthly per 04.1 and formalized quarterly, produces a state reading. The integrated readiness picture maintains a single page — digital or physical — showing date of last rehearsal per compound, current calibration measurements drawn from the per-interlock threshold tables, state assessment, and next planned training investment per compound. The format descends from 00.9's Continuous Situational Picture: one living document, updated on cadence, readable at a glance, truthful. Extreme Ownership supplies the self-assessment discipline that prevents asymmetric-state concealment; Training for the Uphill Athlete supplies the ADS pattern as the canonical weakest-link case; Boyd's OODA frames the recognition layer as the compound's own orient phase at meta-level.

This section installs compound recognition as the diagnostic layer governing all five interlocks. You load the four compound states (ACTIVE / DEGRADING / DORMANT / FAILED) with observable signatures per state, the operational-ceiling rule that the weakest compound defines the ceiling regardless of how strong any individual compound runs, the asymmetric-state concealment hazard where operators overestimate compounds in their favored domain and underestimate compounds in their weak domain, the compound-specific self-perception lag (A ~30 d · B ~90 d · C ~14 d · D ~60 d · E 7–14 d), the quarterly compound review protocol running on fixed calendar date against the integrated readiness picture, the pre-mission compound check scaling mission scope to available compound state, the inverted-pyramid allocation sending 60–70% of training to the weakest compound, and the install / function / failure / feed-forward handoff. Sources: Willink / Babin Extreme Ownership (self-assessment discipline, check the ego); Training for the Uphill Athlete (ADS weakest-link case); Boyd (OODA at meta-level); 00.9 (Continuous Situational Picture template); each interlock's per-section calibration table (04.2–04.6).

04.7.1The four compound states

Every compound reads one of four states at any moment. Intermediate states do not exist — a compound is either running, slipping, silent, or broken.

The four compound states
01ACTIVE — all calibration thresholds hold. Cross-domain narration spontaneous under stress. Last rehearsal within domain-specific refresh window. Observable output matches specification.
02DEGRADING — one or more calibration lines drift below threshold. Cross-domain narration intermittent. Latency climbs. The operator can still produce the output under favorable conditions but fails under stress.
03DORMANT — multiple calibration lines below threshold. Cross-domain narration collapses to single-domain logic. Last rehearsal past window. The compound exists on paper, not in operation.
04FAILED — integration pathway is gone. Output requires reinstallation, not refresh. Rebuild cost at 2 to 5× original install per the compound-pathway decay law.

The transitions are observable, not inferred. ACTIVE → DEGRADING shows up as latency drift first, narration collapse second. DEGRADING → DORMANT shows up as missed rehearsal cadence and audit lapses. DORMANT → FAILED shows up when the operator attempts to run the compound under stress and no integration pathway fires at all. STATE IS OBSERVATIONAL, NOT PERCEPTUAL. The written audit catches the state drift that self-perception misses by the compound-specific lag interval.

04.7.2The operational-ceiling rule

The operator's overall readiness is the minimum state across all five compounds. The ceiling is the floor of the set.

The weakest compound sets the operational ceiling. Four ACTIVE compounds plus one DORMANT compound produces a DORMANT-level deployment envelope, not a near-ACTIVE one.

The law is structural. Every mission worth the compounds engages more than one; the mission that requires only one compound was not a compound-level mission to begin with. A cell running Interlocks C and D at ACTIVE while Interlock E sits at DORMANT produces a tempo under contact that collapses at hour three because the substrate cannot sustain the loop. A household running Interlock B at ACTIVE while Interlock A sits at DORMANT loses its pharmacy on the first pursuit because the operator cannot move the pharmacy under detection. INVESTMENT FLOWS TO THE WEAKEST COMPOUND. The instinct to train the strongest is backwards — it widens the gap between ceiling and floor without raising the ceiling, which remains pinned to the floor.

04.7.3Asymmetric-state concealment and the weakest-domain lead question

Operators systematically overestimate compounds in their favored domain and underestimate compounds in their weak domain. The audit must counter the bias at the question-design level.

The weakest-domain lead question

"Which domain of each compound is my weakest?" — the orienting question. "Which compound am I strongest in?" — the distractor question.

A combatives-native operator rates Interlock E as ACTIVE while the alpine side has gone DORMANT. A navigator-native operator rates Interlock A as ACTIVE while the evasion side degrades silently. The mechanism is attention economics: the strong domain feeds positive feedback (the drill felt sharp, the run felt fast), the weak domain feeds negative feedback (the alpine day felt long, the evasion drill felt exposed). The operator's attention migrates toward the strong domain where feedback is rewarding. The written audit counters this by forcing the weakest-domain lead question first, before any strong-domain reporting can anchor the assessment. Every monthly audit begins with the weakest-domain question per compound; audits that begin with "what went well" systematically miss the compound-specific lag that the self-perception interval was supposed to catch.

04.7.4Compound-specific self-perception lag

Self-perception lags reality by compound-specific intervals. The lag determines how stale the operator's felt-sense of compound state is before the written audit catches it.

Compound-specific self-perception lag
01INTERLOCK A (DETECTION)~30 d · signcutting and route-decision feedback is fast, but evasion signature requires a realistic stressor to surface.
02INTERLOCK B (PHARMACY)~90 d · the seasonal cycle amplifies the drift window; acute clinical work is sparse in a healthy household.
03INTERLOCK C (INFORMATION OODA)~14 d · radio traffic and area-study freshness feed back quickly.
04INTERLOCK D (COMMAND)~60 d · depends on team practice cadence; solo rehearsal cannot substitute.
05INTERLOCK E (PHYSICAL)7–14 d · the fastest feedback; training logs and nose-breathing tests read current state immediately.

The lag determines the minimum audit cadence per compound. Interlock E tolerates a 14 day audit cadence because the lag is short. Interlock B requires a 30 day written audit even though the seasonal loop runs on annual cadence, because the 90 day self-perception lag would otherwise hide drift across the entire acute-presentation window. AUDIT CADENCE RUNS UNIFORMLY AT 30 DAYS ACROSS ALL FIVE COMPOUNDS. The common cadence is conservative against the longest lag, not liberal against the shortest — the operational cost of over-auditing a fast-feedback compound is minutes, while the operational cost of under-auditing a slow-feedback compound is a DORMANT compound discovered mid-mission.

04.7.5The quarterly compound review protocol

The quarterly review is the formal compound-state accounting. It runs on fixed calendar date, non-negotiable.

Quarterly review protocol

01 · INPUTS — training log, after-action debriefs, compound rehearsals since last review. 02 · PER-COMPOUND WALK — walk the per-interlock threshold table (04.2 through 04.6); mark each calibration line; color-code the compound's state. 03 · STATE OUTPUT — ACTIVE / DEGRADING / DORMANT / FAILED per compound. 04 · WEAKEST-DOMAIN IDENTIFICATION — name the weakest domain within each compound, not just the weakest compound. 05 · ONE-HOUR-PER-WEEK INVESTMENT — set the next quarter's target per compound, weighted to weakest-domain-within-weakest-compound. 06 · TEAM REVIEW — for team compounds (especially 04.D), the review is shared with the team.

The integrated readiness picture is updated at review close: single page, one line per compound, showing date of last rehearsal, current state, weakest domain, next investment. The pre-mission compound check runs 10 minutes per compound before any deployment — "if I need this compound tonight, is it ready?" — and if any compound reads DEGRADING or worse on a mission-critical axis, the mission defers, scope adjusts, or a teammate augments the weak compound.

04.7.6The inverted-pyramid allocation

Training investment flows to the weakest compound first. The allocation inverts the pyramid most operators default to.

The default allocation is wrong

Most operators allocate training by comfort and feedback quality: most time to the strongest compound, least to the weakest. This widens the gap between ceiling and floor without raising the ceiling.

The compound allocation law: 60 to 70% of training time to the weakest compound, 30 to 40% across the other four. The strongest compound maintains at floor rather than peak, because even the strongest compound decays when it is not being rehearsed. Rehearsal cadence beats intensity — a compound rehearsed quarterly at moderate intensity retains state better than a compound rehearsed yearly at high intensity. Continuity over episodic. HIGH COMPETENCE IS A FORMER STATE. Compound state is a current-tense property, always. The operator's past capability is not their present capability; the present is what the calendar of rehearsals since the last audit produces.

04.7.7Install, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALLATION PROTOCOL. Build the integrated readiness picture as a single-page living document (descends from 00.9 CSP template). Schedule the monthly audit and quarterly review on fixed calendar dates. Schedule the pre-mission compound check as a mandatory gate before any deployment requiring compound performance. Write the weakest-domain lead question at the top of the audit template. Commit to the inverted-pyramid allocation in advance of the quarter — not as each week's schedule is built.

FUNCTION IN OPERATION. Monthly audit runs on calendar cadence at 10–15 minutes per compound. Quarterly review runs on calendar cadence at 1–2 hours total. Pre-mission check runs at 10 minutes per compound before deployment. Integrated readiness picture updates per review. Training allocation routes 60–70% of weekly training time to the weakest compound.

FAILURE INDICATORS. Audit cadence slips past 45 days. Quarterly review misses the fixed calendar date. Training allocation drifts back to the comfort default (most time to strongest). The operator self-assesses as ACTIVE across all compounds with no weakest-compound identified — a mathematical impossibility, a concealment signature. Pre-mission check skipped; mission launched on felt readiness rather than written state.

FEED-FORWARD. Section 04.8 installs the compound-failure doctrine, naming the three failure modes and the adversary-targeting patterns that attack the integration layer. The recognition layer installed here is the orientation — the failure doctrine is the decision-and-action layer that activates when a compound reads DORMANT or FAILED. The CLOSE hands off to Sub-module 05 SUSTAINMENT, where compound infrastructure maintains the compounds against multi-year horizons.

SECTION 04.8

Compound failure — asymmetric skill, degradation signatures, adversary targeting

Compound failure is a separate doctrine from constituent-skill failure and resolves through a separate protocol. Clausewitz supplies the friction-as-weapon frame; Boyd supplies the tempo-disruption attack vector; Willink and Babin's Extreme Ownership supplies the after-action accountability discipline; the CIA Psychological Operations in Guerrilla Warfare target-audience-analysis method supplies the adversary's compound-mapping logic applied to capability rather than population; Training for the Uphill Athlete supplies the decay curves for aerobic and motor-pattern atrophy; Miller's chemical-cocktail findings explain why stack-dressed-as-compound capabilities fail first under live stress. The compound is capital; failure doctrine is how you defend the capital.

This section installs the three failure modes that every compound in 04 decays through, the weakest-link amplification arithmetic that turns small deficits into compound-level misses, the decay clocks per constituent domain that drive the rehearsal calendar, the four adversary compound-targeting mechanisms that attack the integration layer rather than the constituents, the forty-eight-hour after-action protocol that catches failure before it scars the compound, the asymmetric-rebuild allocation that repairs the weakest domain first, and the three closing laws that govern compound integrity over operational lifespan. Sources: Clausewitz On War Books I and VII (friction, culminating point as failure signature); Boyd (tempo disruption as attack vector); Willink / Babin Extreme Ownership (Laws 1, 2, 11 — root-cause ownership, after-action discipline, Prioritize and Execute under degraded state); CIA PSYOP target-audience analysis (adversary's capability-mapping logic); Training for the Uphill Athlete (aerobic decay curves, detraining physiology); Miller Meditations on Violence (phantom-compound exposure under chemical cocktail); 00.9 Critical-state perception (the audit substrate).

04.8.1Three failure modes

Compound failure does not arrive as a single event. It arrives in one of three distinguishable modes, each with its own signature, its own remediation, and its own cost if misdiagnosed.

Compound failure modes
01SILENT DEGRADATION — one constituent domain decays below threshold while operator self-assessment still reads ACTIVE. Most common mode across all five compounds. Constituent-domain training continues, the operator feels productive, the compound-specific neural pathway goes dark. Detection requires external measurement; internal feel is uninformative.
02ASYMMETRIC COLLAPSE — under live stress the weakest domain fails first, the compound reverts to strongest-single-domain behavior, and the operator continues believing the compound is running while actually running a stack on instinct. Signature: output drops to the ceiling of the single strongest domain, not to zero.
03ADVERSARY-TARGETED — a sophisticated adversary has modeled the compound and attacks its integration mechanism rather than its strongest constituent. Friction is imposed at the seam between domains, not within any one domain. Signature: individual skills test fine in isolation but the interlock will not close under contact.

Each mode demands a different counter. Silent degradation is caught by audit cadence; asymmetric collapse is caught by stressor rehearsal; adversary-targeted collapse is caught by red-team review of the integration layer. MISDIAGNOSIS PRODUCES WRONG REBUILD INVESTMENT. An operator who diagnoses adversary-targeted collapse as silent degradation trains the wrong domains and the integration stays exposed. An operator who diagnoses asymmetric collapse as adversary-targeted over-invests in counter-intelligence while the underlying weakest domain continues to rot.

04.8.2Weakest-link amplification — the compound's internal arithmetic

Within any compound, the weakest domain's deficit cascades through the other two with multiplicative, not additive, effect. The arithmetic is load-bearing for every allocation decision in 05 SUSTAINMENT.

Amplification cascade (detection-compound example)

10% weaker evasion in 04.A → ~40% more detection exposure → ~80% slower route-decision latency → ~100% miss on pursuit timeline. A small deficit at one node produces disproportionately large output deficit at compound level because each downstream stage compounds the upstream error.

The cascade logic holds across every compound. In the pharmacy compound, a ten percent weaker medical differential produces forty percent more wrong-botanical selections, which produces eighty percent higher adverse-outcome rates, which collapses the patient-to-patient trust loop the compound runs on. In the command compound, a ten percent weaker OODA tempo yields forty percent slower orient-phase updates, eighty percent more stale directives, and a hundred percent loss of inner-loop advantage against an adversary cycling at your prior speed. The practical implication is that training volume allocated to the weakest domain produces higher compound-level return than volume allocated to the strongest, at every allocation margin, until the weakest has cleared its minimum threshold. This is the core justification for the inverted-pyramid allocation rule from 04.7.

04.8.3Decay clocks per constituent domain

The rehearsal calendar is driven by the decay physics of each constituent. Every domain has a half-life, every compound has a faster half-life than any of its constituents, and every allocation ignoring these clocks produces silent degradation.

Constituent decay timelines
01MOTOR SKILL (combatives, weapons manipulation, knot work) — measurable decay 14 d of disusesignificant decay 30 d · near-baseline regression 90 d.
02AEROBIC CAPACITY (Zone-2 base, AeT ceiling) — decay onset ~14 drequires 4–12 wk to rebuild once lost, longer when lost deep.
03ANAEROBIC / STRENGTH (power, max force) — decay onset ~7–10 drebuild 2–6 wk given preserved motor pattern.
04COGNITIVE INTEGRATION (compound-specific pathway, cross-domain orient) — decays faster than any constituent skill. First to go silent when cross-domain rehearsal stops. Rebuild cost 2–5× original install per 04.1's law.
05TEAM INTEGRATION — decays rapidly with personnel change, and absent shared rehearsal, regresses even with stable personnel within ~60 d.

The compound's cognitive integration is the fastest-decaying element in the inventory because it has no solo rehearsal equivalent; a runner maintains aerobic base with solo runs, a lifter maintains strength with solo lifts, but an interlock maintains nothing without interlock rehearsal. Calendar asymmetry follows directly: constituent-skill maintenance runs on weekly to monthly cadence, compound rehearsal runs on weekly to monthly cadence as well, and gaps of more than four weeks between compound rehearsals produce disproportionate integration loss even when constituent training continues uninterrupted.

04.8.4Adversary compound-targeting — four mechanisms

A sophisticated adversary targets the compound's integration layer at much lower cost than attritional targeting of constituent domains. Four mechanisms appear repeatedly in the doctrine.

Adversary compound-targeting mechanisms
01COMPOUND-MAPPING INTELLIGENCE — adversary builds a model of the operator's compounds, identifies the weakest link, and concentrates pressure there. CIA PSYOP target-audience-analysis frame applied to capability rather than population. Counter: control the signature that reveals compound structure.
02FRICTION MAXIMIZATION — stressors designed to overload the integration layer rather than the constituent domains. Clausewitzian friction deployed as weapon, not ambient condition. Counter: integration rehearsal under imposed friction; the compound that holds under rehearsal friction holds under adversary friction.
03TEMPO DISRUPTION — force the operator to react faster than the orient layer can update, breaking the loop. Boyd's core attack doctrine. Counter: inner-loop tempo advantage from the compound layer itself; if your inner loop is faster than the adversary can impose, tempo disruption attacks stall.
04DECOY TARGETING — attack the strongest constituent domain to draw training investment there while the compound's integration rots. Counter: audit-driven allocation, not attack-driven allocation.

The implication is structural. COMPOUND DEFENSE IS ORIENTATION-LAYER DEFENSE. Training log, rehearsal cadence, red-team review, and audit protocol are the infrastructure that preserves the compound against a sophisticated adversary. Constituent-skill training, however heavy, fails to defend an integration layer that no one is rehearsing. The adversary's highest-return attack is the one your training plan does not defend against; the defense is to run a training plan whose structure is the compound itself.

04.8.5Forty-eight-hour after-action protocol

Any live or rehearsal failure activates a fixed-window after-action within forty-eight hours. The window is chosen because memory of mode, sequence, and orientation state decays rapidly past that point, and the after-action's value depends on accurate reconstruction.

Compound-failure after-action (48-hour protocol)

STEP 1 · CLASSIFY the failure mode. Silent degradation, asymmetric collapse, or adversary-targeted. STEP 2 · IDENTIFY the weakest domain. This is the root-cause domain, rarely the domain that failed visibly in the moment. STEP 3 · OWN the failure across all three domains per Extreme Ownership Law 1. Language test: no sentence in the after-action blames a single domain in isolation. Correct form: "my pharmacy compound failed because I stopped running the medical-side differential discipline." Incorrect form: "the herbalist gave me a bad dose." STEP 4 · WRITE the rebuild plan. Specific training investment, timeline, re-rehearsal schedule. STEP 5 · ASK the systemic question. Is there a protocol, audit, or cadence change that would have caught this failure earlier. If yes, install the change before the rebuild begins; otherwise the rebuilt compound carries the same blind spot forward.

The asymmetric-rebuild allocation runs for the duration of the rebuild cycle. Instead of thirty-three percent volume across three domains, allocate sixty percent to the weakest, twenty-five percent to the middle, fifteen percent to the strongest, for one four-to-eight-week cycle. Return to balanced allocation once the weakest has cleared its minimum threshold, verified by live rehearsal, not by self-report. Balanced allocation during rebuild preserves the deficit; asymmetric allocation closes it. This is the single most consequential training-plan principle in the compound layer, and it is the principle most often violated in practice because constituent-skill gyms and coaches reward balanced programming.

04.8.6Three laws of compound failure

Three laws govern compound integrity across operational lifespan. They are corollaries of the compound definition in 04.1 applied to the long-horizon failure case.

LAW 1 · Training produces compound; compound produces fate. The operator does not rise to the occasion; the operator defaults to the lowest compound state in inventory. Training-to-contact is deployment of pre-installed compounds, not transfer learning. LAW 2 · Failure in rehearsal is information. Failure under live contact, uncaught and uncorrected, is terminal. The value of compound rehearsal is precisely its capacity to fail safely, and the rehearsal calendar is the operator's only route to compounding failures into asset growth rather than into capital destruction. LAW 3 · Compound integrity is the operator's central strategic asset. Individual skills can be hired, rented, delegated, or retrieved from a manual. Installed compounds cannot; they are capital accumulated across years through the RSI feedback loop, and their protection is the highest-leverage allocation of attention available. A failed compound acknowledged is less damaging than a phantom compound assumed operational, because the acknowledged gap allows planning while the phantom commits the operator to actions the compound cannot support, discovered at the worst possible moment.

The laws compose. Training produces compound, rehearsal protects compound, acknowledgement preserves the capital. An operator who violates any one of the three eventually discovers the violation at live contact, where the cost of discovery is highest and the cost of correction is greatest.

04.8.7Installation, function, failure, feed-forward

INSTALL. Adopt the three-mode failure classification (silent, asymmetric, adversary-targeted) and place it in the training log as a required field for every rehearsal after-action. Write the decay clocks for your five compounds onto the calendar; put minimum rehearsal cadences against each constituent domain and against each compound. Stand up the forty-eight-hour after-action protocol with the five-step sequence and the Extreme-Ownership language test. Install the asymmetric-rebuild allocation (60 / 25 / 15) as the standing response to any identified weakest-domain deficit, replacing balanced programming during rebuild.

FUNCTION. The compound-failure doctrine runs as the complement to compound recognition in 04.7. Where recognition reads state during normal operation, failure doctrine activates when state drops or threatens to drop, classifies the failure mode, diagnoses the weakest domain, and drives the rebuild allocation. The audit cadence (monthly four-question, quarterly stressor rehearsal) produces the early-warning signal; the after-action protocol converts the signal into remediation; the decay clocks calibrate the rehearsal calendar so that expected maintenance catches most decay before it classifies as failure at all.

FAILURE. The doctrine fails when rehearsal friction is insufficient to surface integration-layer weaknesses, when after-actions blame a single domain instead of owning the compound, when rebuild allocation returns to balanced programming before the weakest has cleared threshold, or when the operator treats phantom-compound exposure as acceptable because constituent-skill self-reports are strong. Each of these failure modes converts failure-as-information into failure-as-terminal state by routing around the three laws.

FEED-FORWARD. With compound recognition in 04.7 and compound failure doctrine in 04.8 installed, the acceleration layer is complete. Five compounds running, four feedback architectures active, one audit substrate from 00.9, one diagnostic principle, one recognition cadence, one failure doctrine. The compound is installed, the compound is audited, the compound is defended. Sub-module 05 SUSTAINMENT takes the compound as a capital asset and installs the long-horizon infrastructure — food, tools, preservation, cache, power, continuity — that keeps the capital on the books across multi-year operational horizons.

The acceleration layer is installed. Boyd's OODA loop runs inside four of the five compounds as the tempo engine; Clausewitz's friction, culminating point, and center-of-gravity concepts frame the command compound's operating conditions; Willink and Babin's twelve laws govern the command-under-fire integration and the after-action protocol across all five; the Area Intelligence Handbook's five-phase cycle and F3EAD targeting loop supply the information compound's internal architecture; Training for the Uphill Athlete and Training for the New Alpinism supply the physiological substrate under every compound's physical demand; Dempsey and Miller hold the force compound's grammar and the chemical-cocktail conditions under which every interlock is finally decided. Six doctrinal traditions, one coherent architecture, five installed compounds.

Sub-module 04 installs the compound layer as VOLUME_001's asset class. You now hold five interlocks, each a three-domain closed-loop producing nonlinear output, each calibrated to named thresholds, each audited on a fixed cadence, each defended against a named taxonomy of failure and adversary attack. Detection and counter-detection operates as a dual-cadence signcut-route-signature cycle with nav-first installation, five-to-fifteen-minute active cadence, and track-trap / sensor-asymmetry / baseline-shaping defenses. Self-sufficient pharmacy operates as a nested inner-outer loop with medical-first installation, a twenty-to-thirty-agent pharmacopeia minimum, and three named collapse modes (diagnosis · supply · clinical-judgment). Information-warfare OODA operates on the five-phase intelligence cycle with F3EAD nested inside, Six Layers of OE as the orientation substrate, intel-first installation, and 4GW moral-level centrality. Command under fire operates as a six-beat cycle on an under-contact cadence of ten-to-sixty seconds, governed by the twelve laws, with leadership-first installation and defenses against decapitation, tempo disruption, moral-level undermining, and overextension-trap bait. Operator physical specification operates on a polarized aerobic distribution calibrated to ventilatory thresholds, five periodization principles with TINSTAAFL as the governing law, fitness-first installation, and a five-year continuity horizon against which every mesocycle is evaluated.

Above the five compounds, two meta-layers govern the system. Recognition reads state across the four operational classes, applies the operational-ceiling rule to identify the weakest compound as the capability ceiling, runs the weakest-domain lead question on every audit, accounts for compound-specific self-perception lag, and allocates rebuild volume on the inverted-pyramid. Failure doctrine classifies any degradation into one of three modes, applies the weakest-link amplification arithmetic to the remediation calculus, reads the decay clocks on the rehearsal calendar, identifies the four adversary targeting mechanisms, and runs the forty-eight-hour after-action protocol with the Extreme-Ownership language test. The two meta-layers convert the compound layer from installed capability into defended capital.

The compound is the product. The stack is the sum. Baseline and foundational architecture build additively; acceleration protocols multiply. VOLUME_001 turns on the difference between the two, and the difference between the two is the difference between an operator with skills and an operator with compounds.

The acceleration beat of the RSI progression is closed. Sub-modules 00, 01, and 02 installed the constituents; sub-module 03 installed the force layer; sub-module 04 installed the compounds that interlock all of it into one nonlinear system. Sustainment follows. 05 SUSTAINMENT takes every compound as a capital asset and installs the long-horizon infrastructure each one requires: food production for the physical specification, tool production and preservation for the pharmacy, cache depth and supply architecture for the detection-loop, power and material production for the comms stack, and the homestead continuity discipline that holds all of it against multi-year horizons. Where 04 shows how the skills compound, 05 shows how the compounds persist. 06 COMMAND then runs the compound under doctrine, and 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT indexes the compound into the condition-class matrix that activates it in live environment.

INSTALL. Hold 04 as a system, not as a chapter. Keep the five compounds under monthly four-question audit and quarterly stressor rehearsal. Keep the recognition layer's weakest-domain lead question as the first question of every review. Keep the failure doctrine's forty-eight-hour after-action active against every rehearsal or live failure. Treat any degradation to DORMANT or FAILED as a rebuild allocation trigger, not an administrative note.

FUNCTION. With 04 installed, the operator's capability becomes product rather than sum. Inner-loop tempo beats external-loop tempo. Integrated orientation beats single-domain reasoning. Recursive self-improvement compounds year-over-year at a rate the stack cannot access. Boyd's Law, scaled from fighter-pilot cockpit to operator life.

FAILURE. Skip the compound layer and downstream gains compound on a stack, not a compound. The arithmetic breaks. The RSI progression flattens. 05's sustainment investments run against constituent skills with no interlock to preserve, 06's command doctrine runs against an operator who defaults to single-domain behavior under contact, and 07's field deployment indexes capabilities that fail the removal diagnostic at the moment of activation. The cost of skipping 04 is visible only in live contact, where correction is expensive.

FEED-FORWARD. You hold the acceleration protocols now. The five interlocks, the four feedback architectures, the recognition layer, the failure doctrine, the after-action protocol, the decay-clock-indexed rehearsal calendar. Every subsequent sub-module assumes the compound layer is installed, running, and audited on cadence. 05 SUSTAINMENT begins.
