SECTION 07.2

Perceptual conditions — sign, sound, signature, indicator

Chain count 12 perceptual chains · Primary draw 00.1 tracking · 00.2 auditory/olfactory · 00.3 Seven Target Indicators · 00.4 surveillance typology · 00.7 Personal Awareness · 00.9 Continuous Picture · Cadence 100% transit with 5-and-25 at every halt · 50% active engagement · 100% within 10 min of resolution · Compound trigger two independent triggers in 15 min forces 00.8 to Crisis · Substrate window Appalachian hardwood 2–6 hr · desert sand 30 min · damp forest 12–24 hr

**T**he perceptual class indexes what the operator sees, hears, smells, and tracks. Ground sign, aerial sign, intangible sign, skyline, shine, thermal, pre-attack indicator, surveillance geometry, animal alarm, canine alert, self-check flag — each routes to a named chain that commands a specific subsystem response.

This section installs the twelve perceptual chains, the cross-channel integration rule that forces Crisis mode under two independent triggers inside fifteen minutes, the substrate-dependent track-age window, and the calibration discipline that drops the loop to fifty percent only under active engagement. Sources: the full 00 baseline stack plus 02.8 tracking and 03.1 threat indexing.

07.2.1Fresh ground sign chain

When you cut single fresh ground sign within a two-hour age window per the 00.1 Track Aging mechanism and the direction matches a threat vector from the 00.6 area study, the 00.1 Signcutting Line protocol executes to confirm direction, 00.9 updates the adversary-model layer, 00.8 Modes of Awareness escalates from Alert to Pre-crisis, 02.6 handrail and baseline route planning re-runs to put you off the track line, and 06.6 SALUTE or Tracker Nine-Line pushes to team on PACE Primary. Terminate on direction confirmation or sixty minutes elapsed.

When multiple fresh prints present with stride width greater than yours and toe angle consistent across samples and print depth indicating ruck-and-weapon load per 00.1 gait analysis, the adversary resolves as armed, burdened, grouped. The 00.4 adversary-model layer logs Size, Activity, Location, Time; 03.10 Break-Line-of-Sight primes; 02.6 catching feature identifies for disengagement. Escalate 00.8 to Crisis if contact distance closes under five hundred meters.

07.2.2Aerial and intangible sign chains

When aerial sign registers — broken branch, disturbed cobweb, bark rub, grass pointer per 00.1 — the 00.1 Pointer-Reading protocol confirms direction against at least two additional pointers. Single pointers treat as hypothesis only because obvious direction may be planted. Countertracking deception priors (fishhook, circle, box, figure-eight from 00.9) activate as cross-check.

When intangible sign arrives — smoke, cooking odor, voice, gear clatter, animal alarm, sudden insect silence per 00.2 — the 00.2 Auditory Signal Categories log the class. Olfactory range estimates distance (cigar smoke around half a mile in favorable weather, canine detection beyond ten miles). 00.9 updates adversary-bearing estimate. The team goes to the 00.2 Sound Discipline Drill with taped gear and slow fluid movement. 00.8 forces Pre-crisis. Any voice heard reads as human adversary until ruled out, because voice is species-identifying regardless of language.

07.2.3Signature and skyline chains

SKYLINE / SILHOUETTE — go immediately behind vertical cover, never walk the ridgeline, load 03.6 IMT low-crawl or high-crawl
OPTICAL GLINT / SHINE — treat bearing as surveillance OP until disproven, cue NAI on bearing, kill-flash on own optics, update 03.9 Range Card
THERMAL — nasal-only breathing for steam suppression, matte overspray, thermal cloak if in kit, abort on heat-illness threshold

When a skyline or silhouette appears on ridge, lit window, or moonlit horizon per 00.3, you go immediately behind vertical cover, never walk the ridgeline, and 03.6 Individual Movement Techniques load low crawl or high crawl per the 00.3 Seven Target Indicators scan.

When optical glint, glass flash, or metal shine registers beyond fifty meters per 00.3 Shine subtypes, treat the bearing as a surveillance observation post until disproven. 00.9 cues a Named Area of Interest on that bearing. 00.1 Kill-Flash on own optics verifies. 03.9 Range Card updates if static. 06.6 SALUTE pushes the bearing with Body/Form/Demeanor/Longevity items per 00.4.

When your own thermal scan flags a signature or when the 00.6 area study names Color-IR imaging as a threat, 00.3 thermal-evasion protocols activate — nasal-only breathing for steam suppression, black-fabric avoidance, matte overspray, thermal cloak if in kit with documented ninety-percent reduction. The chain degrades when internal temperature inside the cloak crosses heat-illness threshold from 01.7.

07.2.4Pre-Attack Indicator Cascade

When the Pre-Attack Indicator Cascade from 00.4 resolves — a person's path converges with yours without environmental reason — 00.8 goes Pre-crisis. The 00.7 Engagement-Ring Self-Test runs (zero to twenty-five meters close, greater than twenty-five long). 03.1 Interview-to-Attack priors load. 03.6 RTR primes if range compresses. 03.10 enforces the Absence-Evasion-De-escalation-Force hierarchy from the lowest rung.

A person's path converges with yours without environmental reason. That is the entire indicator. Everything else is confirmation.

07.2.5Surveillance geometry

When surveillance geometry confirms — same face, different context, across three or more observations within twenty-four hours per 00.4 Surveillance Typology — the Density-Determines-Distance rule applies (crowd three to five meters, sparse twenty to one hundred-plus). 00.4 Gray Man activates. 06.4 Daily Intelligence Check-Up notes the pattern. Route varies through 02.6 handrail alternation. Habit timing is immaterial under active surveillance — immediate route and posture change override.

07.2.6Animal alarm and canine alert

When the animal alarm bank activates — deer snort, corvid chatter, insect silence — assume human presence on the alarm bearing and cue 00.1 Signcutting Line. The fauna react to what you have not yet detected.

When your own K-9 or local dogs alert on wind bearing, 00.2 olfactory-range estimate runs. Scent-sanitation discipline reviews (twenty-four hours of food discipline, UV brightener check). The canine nose operates at six to ten miles under favorable conditions — the dog is a better detector than the operator.

07.2.7Self-check flag

When your 00.7 photographic self-check flags a shadow cast beyond cover, shine from optic, or spacing under three linear feet on camo, the chain halts all movement until the 00.3 contrast-reversal face paint is reapplied and kill-flash verifies. The self-check is the operator auditing his own signature before the adversary audits it.

07.2.8Cross-channel integration

WARN

Two independent perceptual triggers inside a fifteen-minute window force 00.8 to Crisis regardless of individual trigger severity. A single trigger is an observation; two is a pattern; the pattern is the decisive signal.

The chain degrades when reporting reduces to single-channel language. Cross-channel integration is the compound-ACTIVE signature for 04.2 Detection/Counter-Detection Loop.

07.2.9Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the perceptual chain through the 5-and-25 Meter Drill at every halt, the substrate-name-before-age-name discipline, and u the named-class-before-named-response reflex u.

It functions when cross-channel triggers integrate automatically, when cadence drops only under active engagement, and when the substrate window calibrates track-age readings.

It fails when single-channel reporting replaces integration, when cadence drops for comfort rather than combat, or when substrate is assumed rather than read.

Perceptual feeds forward into 07.3 Environmental — the two classes often stack and force compound chain activation.

SECTION 07.3

Environmental conditions — terrain, weather, light, water, fire

Chain count 14 environmental chains · Primary draw 01.2 shelter/thermal · 01.3 fire · 01.4 water · 01.7 environmental injury · 02.5 Naismith · 02.6 handrail · 02.9 FOTH · 05.8 fire regime · Thermal threshold 0°C static > 20 min = CRITICAL · 30°C + 2 hr load = heat-illness priors · Terrain scaling Class 3 doubles Naismith · glaciated triples · Light buffer 30 min to last light for shelter · 60 min adverse weather · Altitude negligible < 2400 m · acclimatize 2400–3000 · pre-acclimate 3000–4300 · oxygen > 4300

**Environmental chains route off terrain, temperature, precipitation, light condition, season, altitude, snow state, fire regime, and water state. The thermal chains run first because thermoregulation will kill faster than immobility**.

This section installs the cold-stack and heat-stack chains, the Class 3/4 terrain scaling against Naismith, the avalanche and glacier protocols from FOTH, the time-to-dark calculation that commands shelter over travel, and the water-state procurement and crossing logic. Sources: 01.2 through 01.8 primary systems, 02.5 Naismith, 02.6 handrail, 02.9 FOTH chapters, 05.8 Firewise.

07.3.1Cold-weather static chain

When ambient temperature drops below zero Celsius and operator goes static beyond twenty minutes, 01.2 runs the Four Modes of Heat Loss assessment across conduction, convection, radiation, and evaporation. 01.2 COLD enforces clean, overheating-avoided, loose-and-layered, dry. The three-layer cold-weather clothing verifies. 01.2 debris-hut or tarp-wedge primitive shelter cues if the halt exceeds sixty minutes. 01.3 fire-craft loads the ferro-rod plus tinder hierarchy. A raised-platform bed builds if overnight because two hours of ground contact loses more heat than air.

When that same sub-zero temperature combines with precipitation — cold rain being the worst case under 01.2's cotton-kills law — and shelter is not yet built, 01.2 executes at PRIORITY over 02-TRAVERSE. 01.1 STOP pauses movement. Shelter completes within ninety minutes of degradation onset because shivering is a countdown rather than a shield. 00.9 logs environmental class as CRITICAL.

07.3.2Heat-stress chain

When ambient temperature rises above thirty Celsius and operator sustains load beyond two hours, 01.7 heat-illness priors load. The 01.1 water-loss rate around a liter per hour in desert heat informs the 01.4 Field Water-Decision Protocol. Water splits across containers per 05.1 BOB logic. 02.10 pace drops to the AeT zone because heat compounds heart-rate drift.

07.3.3Cold-weather casualty

When a cold-weather casualty presents per 01.7 hypothermia staging, 01.6 MARCH modifies — hypothermia prevention becomes primary because the lethal triad of hypothermia, acidosis, and coagulopathy overrides fluid-resuscitation priority. Casualty shelter builds IMMEDIATE. Rewarming stays cautious because rapid external rewarming of the severely hypothermic can kill. The no-one-dead-until-warm-and-dead law enforces.

07.3.4Terrain class chains

CLASS 3 — hands needed, loose grade, bouldersFOTH Ten Essentials verifypace drops · Naismith doubles
CLASS 4 — minimum 3-person rope teamanchor and belay disciplinepre-computed compass and map bearings
CANALIZATION — valley / ravine / gulchroute high not lowHopkins ambush-terrain read · KOCOA before descent
AVALANCHE — 30–45° slope with snow loadingbeacon/probe/shovel triadsingle-slope crossing with spot safe zones

When Class 3 enters, 02.9 FOTH Ten Essentials verify, pace expectation drops, 02.5 Naismith recalibrates to double-Naismith, and 02.9 self-arrest primes if snow or ice is present. When Class 4 enters, 02.9 calls a minimum three-person rope team. Anchor and belay discipline loads. 02.2 compass bearing plus 02.1 map bearing pre-compute before you step into exposed ground.

When a valley, ravine, or gulch registers as canalization risk under 00.5 plus Hopkins's ambush-terrain read from 03.8, 02.6 routes high rather than low. 03.8 canalizing-blocking-turning-slowing terrain reading activates. 03.6 cover-versus-concealment discrimination enforces. 03.9 KOCOA runs before descent.

07.3.5Avalanche and glacier chains

When avalanche terrain registers at thirty to forty-five degrees slope with snow loading per FOTH Chapter 17, 02.9 Avalanche Safety Triad (beacon, probe, shovel) verifies. The beacon-search protocol rehearses. The fifteen-minute burial survival window informs response cadence. The team crosses single slopes one at a time with spot safe zones above and below.

On glacier, 02.9 rope-team travel loads with crevasse-rescue hardware on harness. Plunge step and kick step default. The three-person minimum rope team holds because the two-person configuration is the weakest under 02.9 doctrine.

07.3.6Light and season chains

When time-to-dark falls under ninety minutes and shelter is unresolved, 01.2 shelter protocol executes at PRIORITY over 02-TRAVERSE. The 01.3 fire-lay pre-builds in daylight. 00.9 briefs light discipline for night posture.

When night falls without moon, 00.3 light discipline goes strict. 02.2 USMC Lensatic compass night-navigation loads if movement continues. 02.8 night tracking runs (often better than day due to low-angle light on prints). NVG adversary priors register because an IR laser visible to NVG is invisible to friendlies.

07.3.7Seasonal stack chains

When winter, snow, and boreal forest stack, 01.3 loads the three-tinder tree set (birch bark, pine fatwood, resinous conifer duff). 01.2 super-shelter or Yukon-stove-in-wedge builds. The 02.9 snow-travel toolset loads.

When summer stacks with dry fuel load, 05.8 Firewise zones assess around any static position. 01.3 shifts to smokeless discipline with curfew and banking. Wildfire evacuation PACE pre-loads.

07.3.8Water-state chains

When flowing water and water need coincide, 01.4 Field Water-Decision runs — pre-filtration before treatment because clarity is not safety, the treatment hierarchy holds (boil beats chemical beats filter), and long-term storage uses silver plus activated carbon.

When a water crossing is required, 01.7 HELP position loads if deep or cold. The Reach-Throw-Tow-Go rescue hierarchy prioritizes. 06.6 PACE pre-positions on each bank. Gear waterproofing verifies that 05.1 BOB water-split logic survives immersion.

When terrain floods, 02-TRAVERSE re-routes (no catching feature is reliable in flood under 02.6). 02.7 SAR lost-person behavior shifts because people under water stress move differently. 01.4 four-class pathogen discipline governs drinking.

07.3.9Fire and altitude chains

When active wildfire or smoke plume appears, 05.8 rules echo — do not move uphill into smoke. 01.2 shelter priorities re-weight for thermal and respiratory protection. 05.8 Firewise zones determine shelter-in-place versus evacuation. 06.9 grid-dependence check flags water-pump failure.

DEF

ALTITUDE BANDS — negligible below 2,400 m; acclimatize 2,400–3,000 m; pre-acclimate and climb-high-sleep-low at 3,000–4,300 m; rigorous acclimatization with oxygen-saturation monitoring above 4,300 m.

07.3.10Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the environmental chain through the naming discipline (temperature band, terrain class, light window named before activation), the thermal-first reflex (thermoregulation precedes every other environmental chain), and the Naismith recalibration on load, class, and weather.

It functions when the chain fires cleanly on threshold crossings, when priority over 02-TRAVERSE holds under CRITICAL environmental load, and when the fire regime reads as a variable rather than a constant.

It fails when thermoregulation defers to travel ambition, when Class 3-4 terrain enters without rope-team preparation, or when altitude bands are ignored.

Environmental feeds forward into 07.4 — adversarial conditions frequently exploit environmental CRITICAL to compress the operator's options.

theFIELD.run / CONSTRUCT_APPLICATIONS / 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT / 07.4 Adversarial conditions — pre-contact, contact, numbers, permissiveness
SECTION 07.4

Adversarial conditions — pre-contact, contact, numbers, permissiveness

Hierarchy of Response Avoidance · Escape · De-escalate · Counter-assault · Close engagement 0–25 m · Mid range 25–300 m · Beyond 300 m+ · HR bands < 115 fine motor · 115–145 gross motor peak · > 145 cognitive narrowing · > 175 shutdown · Numbers ladder single · pair · fire team (3–5) · squad-plus (5+) · Permissiveness bands permissive · semi-permissive · non-permissive · Force calibration Miller-Kane Level 1–6 · Pre-attack rule Absence > De-escalation > Force

**P**re-contact chains run first because absence beats every kinetic response. Contact chains calibrate by distance band. Numbers chains scale force architecture. Permissiveness scales the full stack across peacetime, civil unrest, and active combat.

This section installs the 03.1 Hierarchy of Response, the distance-band contact ladder from close engagement to mid-range to beyond three hundred meters, the numbers-scaled force architecture from single adversary through squad-plus, the three-band permissiveness calibration, and the ambush-and-defense protocols from 03.8 and 03.9. Sources: 03 in full (Meditations on Violence, Facing Violence, Scaling Force, SEAL Survival Guide, Ranger Handbook, Armalite Rifle Manual, Hopkins, Dolio, TW-03), 00.4, 06.3.

07.4.1Interview-to-Attack cascade

When the 03.1 Interview-to-Attack cascade resolves — stranger closes distance, asks a diversion question, positions for brush contact — the 03.1 Hierarchy of Response enforces from the lowest rung (Avoidance, Escape, De-escalate, Counter-assault). 03.10 Break-Line-of-Sight primes if avoidance requires movement. 03.2 IMOP (Intent, Means, Opportunity, Preclusion) runs as mental checklist. 00.8 goes Pre-crisis. 03.2 Performance-by-Heart-Rate priors load because fine motor degrades above one-hundred-forty-five bpm.

07.4.2Predator type chains

RESOURCE PREDATOR — hierarchy defaults to comply-and-disengage for replaceable resources; force escalates only if compliance fails to terminate
PROCESS PREDATOR — the attack itself is the goal; compliance fails outright; Four Basic Truths of Assault apply; Hit Hard or Don't Hit governs
CHARM PREDATOR — social setup disguising violence intent; break the script immediately; Gray Man reinforces; Cooper's Orange activates

When the threat is a Resource Predator under 03.1, the hierarchy defaults to comply-and-disengage for replaceable resources and escalates to force only if compliance fails to terminate. 03.3 Miller-Kane Force Continuum scales response to threat level with documentation.

When the threat is a Process Predator — the attack itself being the goal — compliance fails outright. 03.1 Four Basic Truths of Assault apply (attacks are close, fast, from unexpected angle, by surprise). 03.3 Hit Hard or Don't Hit governs. 03.2 Golden Rule of Combat (do not be where the attack is) holds. 03.10 plus Level 1-2 Scaling Force E&E anchors the exit.

07.4.3Surveillance-confirmed chain

When surveillance confirms at three-plus face-context repetitions in twenty-four hours, 00.4 Gray Man fully activates with vehicle Four Ps discipline. Route randomization against daisy-chain surveillance runs. 06.6 PACE shifts to alternate channel. 04.2 Detection/Counter-Detection Loop engages as active compound.

07.4.4Close engagement (0–25 m)

At zero to twenty-five meters in the close engagement ring from 00.7, 03.6 RTR immediate (Return fire, Take cover, Return effective fire). 03.3 Dempsey Semi-Crouch plus the Falling-Step Trigger Cascade handles empty-hand. 03.4 SEAL Seven plus the 3 D's (Definition, Direction, Drive) handles armed engagement. 03.10 Break-Line-of-Sight executes within five seconds if retreating. 01.6 MARCH primes for casualty response. 06.6 ACE report (Ammo, Casualty, Equipment) pushes immediately post-contact.

07.4.5Mid-range engagement (25–300 m)

At twenty-five to three hundred meters, 03.4 carbine stance selects for terrain. Natural Point of Aim and Bone Support load. 03.6 cover-versus-concealment discrimination enforces (cover stops rounds; concealment only obscures). 03.7 Fire-and-Movement runs five-second bounds per IMT doctrine. 03.9 SALT plus SALUTE pushes to higher.

07.4.6Beyond 300 m

Beyond three hundred meters, Fundamental-Accuracy dominates. 03.7 Traveling Overwatch or Bounding Overwatch engages. 03.8 Engagement-Priorities Matrix applies if own ambush is initiating (Hopkins priorities run crew-served > leaders > comms > rest). 03.9 Range Card updates.

When ambushed — linear, L, V, Z, Y, X per 03.8 — 03.7 Dolio civilian default Break Contact executes. Direction of fire identifies. Movement runs perpendicular to the L-ambush long axis or reverse from the linear ambush. 03.6 IMT selects per cover. 03.10 counter-tracking (fishhook, circle, box, figure-eight per 00.9) runs on retreat.

07.4.7Numbers-scaled force architecture

SINGLE — 03.1 Hierarchy, Miller-Kane Level 4 or below most cases
PAIR — Buddy-Pair Building Block against you; gain angular separation, force attention split; 03.8 Flanking if you have support
FIRE TEAM (3–5) — one-moves-one-watches leapfrog; Dolio civilian Break Contact; re-engage only if cornered
SQUAD-PLUS (5+) — 03.10 E&E primary; DOCA favors trained light infantry; disperse first, orient, re-concentrate on tactical advantage

07.4.8Permissiveness scaling

In permissive peacetime with friendly populace, 03.10 Absence defaults (03.1 law: best self-defense is not being there). 03.3 force thresholds tune to proportional response. 06.5 legitimacy discipline holds (every act is propaganda, even in peacetime). 06.4 Cooper's Color runs Yellow baseline.

In semi-permissive — civil unrest, failing state, riot zone — 00.4 Gray Man fully activates. 06.6 PACE reduces to essential comms. 03.9 Concentric Rings defense holds at any static location. 06.3 light-footprint-deep-root blends into population.

In non-permissive — active combat, hostile regime, kidnap zone — every movement runs under the 04.2 compound. 03.10 E&E kit carries continuously. 06.6 enforces brevity and frequency agility and DF-mitigation through mobile transmission. 00.6 Area Study updates daily minimum. 06.3 Jaeger mindset installs.

07.4.9Ambush-and-defense calibration

Own-side ambush planning follows 03.8 Hopkins 7-Step Schoolhouse as baseline linear, with L-formation preferred because enfilade fire beats linear geometry. The Three Ambush Elements (assault, support, security) pre-assign. Violence of Action executes inside the 60-Second Rule in kill zone. Claymore employment respects Surface Danger Zone if in kit.

Own-side defense runs 03.9 Dolio Concentric Rings with KOCOA first, Range Card built, Fighting Position Standards per TW-03 Chapter 3, and Observation Post standards per TW-03 Chapter 4 for twenty-four-hour coverage. Miller-Kane Level 1 through 6 calibrates Presence, Voice, Touch, Compliance, Injurious, Lethal, with IMOP satisfied at each step.

WARN

The force chain degrades when the operator cannot articulate IMOP satisfaction at each escalation and FAILS when force applies outside Miller-Kane proportionality. Heart rate above 145 bpm degrades fine motor; above 175 bpm collapses cognition. Train for the bands you will operate in, not the bands you wish you operated in.

07.4.10Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the adversarial chain through three habits. Name IMOP before escalating force. Name the distance band before selecting the contact technique. Name the permissiveness level before planning movement.

It functions when Absence beats every kinetic response, when force calibrates cleanly to Miller-Kane Level with IMOP satisfied, and when u the operator accepts that the best engagement is the one that did not happen u.

It fails when IMOP is assumed rather than articulated, when distance-band technique is mis-selected, or when permissiveness is read from the operator's preference rather than the ground.

Adversarial feeds forward into 07.5 — resource-class degradation frequently appears during or after adversarial engagement.

SECTION 07.5

Resource conditions — supply, grid, water, comms, tools

Grid bands flicker (< 4 hr) · regional (> 24 hr) · HEMP/Blackout · Supply depth ladder 72 hr baseline kit · 7-day local cache · 30-day household · > 30-day homestead production · Water rainwater 1 in × 1000 sqft ≈ 600 gal minus 15–25% · silver + activated carbon long storage · PACE ladder Primary → Alternate → Contingency → Emergency · Rule of Threes applied inverted to stockpileshortest deprivation tolerance, deepest stockpile priority

**R**esource chains route off infrastructure integrity, stockpile depth, water-system state, comms posture, and tool inventory. The five variables are tracked continuously because infrastructure is a dynamic asset, not a constant.

This section installs the three-band grid-collapse chain, the stockpile depth ladder across 72 hours, 7 days, 30 days, and beyond 30 days, the water-procurement protocol under municipal-system failure, the PACE-ladder step-down under comms degradation, and the tool-inventory audit that keeps capability current. Sources: 01.3 fire, 01.4 water, 05.1 through 05.10 sustainment, 06.6 PACE, 06.9 Blackout Warfare.

07.5.1Grid flicker (< 4 hr)

When a grid flicker or local outage stays under four hours, the 06.9 individual-and-family grid-independence audit runs baseline — fridge doors closed, no panic draw from freezer. 05.6 generator holds as non-negotiable backup if duration crosses four hours. The 05.5 three-day water stockpile (Rule of Threes applied to storage per 05.2) verifies.

07.5.2Regional grid collapse (> 24 hr)

When regional grid collapse exceeds twenty-four hours, 06.9 social-order gradient priors load (looting, curfew, refugee flow). 05.6 engages three off-grid energy streams sequentially — solar primary, generator backup, wood-gas and biodiesel tertiary — because any one energy chain will fail and you build three. 05.5 rainwater catchment and stored water prioritize over municipal (assumed compromised). 03.9 Concentric Rings security posture raises at homestead. 06.4 Daily Intelligence Check-Up shifts to battery-radio schedule. 06.6 PACE steps through Primary (family and neighbor), Alternate (regional repeater), and Contingency (HF nets if licensed).

07.5.3HEMP / Blackout Warfare indicators

When HEMP or Blackout Warfare indicators fire per 06.9 four vectors (cyber, physical sabotage, NNEMP, HEMP), Faraday-protected electronics deploy. 05.6 wood-gas and biodiesel become primary because semiconductor systems assume compromise. 05.9 homestead architecture (root cellar, solar pit greenhouse, water catchment) becomes the full operating environment. 06.3 4GW light-footprint-deep-root dominates any external engagement. 05.10 three horizons evaluate current position.

07.5.4Stockpile depth chain

7-day drawdown — FIFO rotation verifies, food production cues, root-cellar loads, BOB review moves forward
72-hour threshold — emergency food production + foraging, Universal Edibility Test + Warnock 276-species ID, Rule of Threes governs, multi-location cache access
Cache compromised — treat as enemy-accessible, no direct approach, Signcutting Line confirms, assume contaminated/trapped
Tool degrades — field sharpening or forge work, alternate fire method from hierarchy, primitive filtration if filter gone

When the stockpile draws down to seven days, 05.2 FIFO rotation verifies (oldest stock first). 05.3 food production cues (planting, harvest, wild-harvest per season). 05.4 root-cellar and preservation infrastructure loads. 05.1 BOB review moves forward even if biannual timing has not elapsed.

When stockpile hits the seventy-two-hour threshold — Rule of Threes applied to storage — 05.3 emergency food production and foraging run simultaneous with 01.5 Universal Edibility Test and Warnock 276-species ID. 01.1 Rule of Threes governs (three weeks without food as hard limit, performance degrading much sooner). 05.2 multi-location distribution at secondary cache accesses. 06.6 PACE informs network of resource state if operationally safe.

07.5.5Compromised cache

When a cache reads known-compromised — disturbed, observed, or over twelve months without verification — the cache treats as enemy-accessible. You do not approach directly. 00.1 Signcutting Line confirms. 04.2 Detection/Counter-Detection runs on approach route. Supplies assume contaminated or trapped until verified. 06.6 PACE notifies team that the cache is offline.

07.5.6Water infrastructure

When municipal water drops, 05.5 Rainwater volumetric rule (one inch of rain times one thousand square feet of roof approximates six hundred gallons minus fifteen-to-twenty-five percent gutter and first-flush loss) computes against roof area. 01.4 Harvesting H2O procurement chain activates — catchment, pre-filter, boil at altitude-corrected time per 05.5, store. 01.4 silver plus activated carbon holds long-storage beyond seven days. 05.5 cellar drainage cross-checks against water-diversion integrity.

When only surface water remains, 01.4 four-class pathogen assessment runs. Clearer is not safer (muddy can be safer than clear). The treatment hierarchy enforces. 01.4 transpiration bag or solar still loads if catchment fails.

07.5.7PACE step-down

When Primary drops, Alternate activates immediately with net discipline preserved (NCS, schedule, authentication). The 05.1 spare antenna and backup battery (Build the Perfect BOB baseline) verify. When all radio channels drop, 06.6 Contingency engages via written messages at courier or physical rendezvous. Emergency runs pre-arranged rendezvous point and time per 06.6 doctrine.

When DF detection is suspected, 06.6 Radio OPSEC keeps transmissions short, irregular, and mobile during transmission. Physical location moves before sustained transmission. Brevity beats encryption in most fieldable cases through scheduled burst and frequency rotation.

07.5.8Long-horizon sustainment

Long-horizon sustainment at 05.10 greater than thirty days or greater than one year loads 05.3 food production (oak savanna, six forest layers, silvopasture per Restoration Agriculture), 05.4 root-cellar and solar pit greenhouse (cool, above-freezing, humid per Storey A-76), 05.6 three energy chains, 05.7 forge plus heat-treat, 05.8 Six Woodland Rules, 05.9 homestead architecture, and 05.10 skills-ladder maintenance.

DEF

STOCKPILE LADDER — 72-hour baseline kit, 7-day local cache, 30-day household, > 30-day homestead production. Rule of Threes inverts: the shortest deprivation tolerance gets the deepest stockpile priority.

07.5.9Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the resource chain through quarterly 72-hour tests, annual 30-day drills, annual one-year paper walkthroughs, and biannual BOB reviews anchored to daylight-savings events.

It functions when the three energy chains run in rotation, when PACE step-down executes automatically on Primary loss, and when tool inventory audits catch degradation before the field catches it.

It fails when a single energy chain is assumed sufficient, when compromised cache is approached directly, or when the stockpile ladder is anchored to convenience rather than deprivation tolerance.

Resource feeds forward into 07.6 — physiological conditions degrade sharply when resource infrastructure collapses.

SECTION 07.6

Physiological conditions — self-state, trauma, environmental injury, mass casualty

Chain precedence MARCH non-negotiable · massive hemorrhage in minutes · TCCC phases Care Under Fire · Tactical Field Care · Tactical Evacuation Care · Pain Ladder OTC · partial agonist · full agonist · Triage START · SALT (walking · immediate · expectant) · Re-MARCH every 15 min Prolonged Field Care · SOAP every 30 min · Environmental hypothermia staged rewarming · heat stroke cold-water immersion · frostbite no refreeze · altitude descent · Floor no-one-dead-until-warm-and-dead

**Self-state chains run first because Personal Awareness is the calibration layer for every other awareness in the stack. Acute trauma runs the MARCH** sequence. Environmental injury runs cautious. Mass casualty triages. Psychological state handles freeze, panic, and post-crisis arousal.

This section installs the 00.7 self-state chain, the MARCH acute-trauma sequence with its permissive-hypothermia and hypothermia-prevention discipline, the Prolonged Field Care cycle, the environmental-injury protocols under the lethal-triad law, and the triage and psychological-state chains. Sources: 00.7 Personal Awareness, 01.6 MARCH, 01.7 environmental injury, 01.8 pain and pharmacy, 02.10 training cycle, 04.E substrate.

07.6.1Self-state chain

When 00.7 PA flags fatigue, injury, cognitive load, medication, or sleep deficit, 00.9 situational-picture weighting reduces until PA restores. 02.10 sleep, nutrition, and recovery infrastructure activates. 04.E substrate checks through the 02.10 Zone 2 nose-breathing test as quick diagnostic.

When emotional hijack detects — anger, fear cresting, arrogance — 00.7 Extreme Ownership self-audit runs. 06.2 Detachment ("high port" mechanism per Willink — step back physically, elevate attention mechanically) engages. 00.8 mode re-centers to Alert before action. 03.2 Golden Rule holds (do not be where the emotion puts you).

When post-crisis arousal persists beyond thirty minutes after event resolution, the return-to-Alert drill enforces — slow breath, 5-and-25 scan from 00.9, named inventory of current context. 00.7 debrief defers to stable state. 01.7 self-check runs for adrenaline-masked injury.

07.6.2MARCH acute trauma

M — Massive Hemorrhage CAT tourniquet 2–3 in above wound, time markedwound packing + direct pressure > 3 min for truncal/junctional
A — Airway position airwayNPA if kit available (not basilar skull fx)jaw-thrust for unconscious with c-spine
R — Respirations chest seal (vented or 3-sided flutter)monitor tension pneumothorax (JVD, trach deviation, unilateral breath loss)needle-decompress per TCCC
C — Circulation secondary bleeding sweeppulse-quality check (radial present ≈ SBP > 90)permissive hypotension
H — Hypothermia prevention criticaltrauma casualty loses heat 3× normallethal triad governs

When a casualty presents compressible arterial hemorrhage, 01.6 MARCH M executes — CAT tourniquet two to three inches above wound, time marked. If truncal or junctional, wound packing with hemostatic gauze plus direct pressure three-plus minutes. Massive hemorrhage first, always, under 01.6 law — with 00.9 five-meter scene security simultaneous (one responder treats, one watches).

07.6.3Post-MARCH tactical permission

If tactical situation permits, 01.6 PAWS secondary runs (Pain management, Antibiotics, Wounds dressed, Splinting). SAMPLE history records. 06.6 CASEVAC 9-line assembles. 06.6 PACE pushes to evacuation asset.

If evacuation window is unclear, 01.7 Prolonged Field Care triggers — re-MARCH every fifteen minutes, hydration oral if tolerated under the conscious-plus-radial-pulse rule, analgesia via 01.8 Pain Ladder (OTC to partial agonist to full agonist), three stages of shock monitoring, SOAP note discipline every thirty minutes.

07.6.4Hypothermia chain

Hypothermia per 01.7 staging (mild, moderate, severe, cardiac arrest) rewarms gradually from trunk outward. Rapid external rewarming of severe hypothermic precipitates afterdrop or VF. CPR continues until warmed under the no-one-dead-until-warm-and-dead law.

WARN

The severely hypothermic patient appears dead and is not. Rewarm gradually from trunk outward. Never assume death until warm-and-dead has been reached and CPR has continued through the rewarming cycle.

07.6.5Heat-stroke and frostbite chains

Exertional heat stroke (core above forty Celsius, altered mental status) runs immediate cooling (cold-water immersion if available, otherwise evaporative plus fanning). Airway protection. IV access if available. TCCC continuing if trauma co-presents.

Frostbite rewarms only when refreeze cannot occur. No rubbing. Pain management loads through 01.8.

07.6.6Altitude illness

Altitude illness (AMS to HACE to HAPE per FOTH Chapter 21) treats through descent as definitive. Acetazolamide prophylaxis considers on high-risk ascent per 02.10. HACE runs immediate descent plus dexamethasone if available. HAPE runs immediate descent plus oxygen plus nifedipine if available.

07.6.7Mass-casualty triage

When three-plus casualties present with two-or-fewer responders, 01.6 triage runs START or SALT — walking wounded to delayed, non-walking breathing to immediate versus expectant by pulse and GCS, non-breathing after airway opened to expectant. 06.8 span-of-control applies with one responder leading and team delegating via the fire-team model. 06.6 9-line CASEVAC runs per patient with precedence (urgent, priority, routine).

07.6.8Psychological state

Freeze observed in self or teammate under 03.2 cues simplest reflex action, loud verbal command, and physical contact. 06.2 Relax-Look-Around-Make-a-Call engages. 03.2 HR awareness brings rate down with exhale before further decision.

Civilian panic cascade at scene triggers 06.7 Leadership forward with Commander's Intent in one sentence ("We're moving to X, follow me"), Simple enforced in all communication, and 03.9 Concentric Rings for crowd management if static.

07.6.9Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the physiological chain through MARCH sequence memorization to automaticity, Prolonged Field Care drills across fifteen-minute cycles, and the tourniquet-time-marking reflex.

It functions when massive hemorrhage treats first, when hypothermia prevention runs on every trauma casualty regardless of ambient temperature, and when u MARCH fires in order without reprioritization by felt severity u.

It fails when MARCH skips a step, when tourniquet removes prematurely, or when hypothermia prevention omits from a bleeding casualty (lethal triad).

Physiological feeds forward into 07.7 — temporal conditions modulate the depth and cadence of every physiological chain.

← PREVIOUS07.5 Resource conditions — supply, grid, water, comms, toolsNEXT →07.7 Temporal conditions — horizon, extraction window, cadence, training cycle

theFIELD.run / CONSTRUCT_APPLICATIONS / 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT / 07.7 Temporal conditions — horizon, extraction window, cadence, training cycle
SECTION 07.7

Temporal conditions — horizon, extraction window, cadence, training cycle

Engagement horizons < 5 min (OODA dominant) · 5–60 min (React-to-Contact) · 1–24 hr (Decentralized Command) · Extraction windows < 30 min (MARCH + 9-line) · 24–72 hr (Prolonged Field Care) · no extraction (04.B + 06.3) · Sustained bands 1–7 d · 1–4 wk · > 1 mo · > 1 yr · Rule of Threes 3 min air · 3 hr shelter · 3 d water · 3 wk food · Habit 8-day conscious-drop · 21-day formed · 100-day automatic · Compound drift aerobic 2 wk · combatives 30 d · alpine 90 d · strength 7 d

**A**cute engagement chains route by time horizon. Extraction-window chains route by asset availability. Sustained-operation chains route by horizon band. Cadence chains route by engagement rhythm. Habit-formation chains route by installation stage. Time-to-dark chains route by light window.

This section installs the five horizon bands across acute engagement, extraction, sustained operation, cadence, and habit formation, the Rule of Threes calibration across air, shelter, water, and food deprivation, the compound-drift clock that names decay rates per capability domain, and the time-to-dark priority rule. Sources: 00.8 OODA/Modes, 01.1 Rule of Threes, 01.7 Prolonged Field Care, 02.5 Naismith, 02.10 training cycle, 05.10 three horizons, 06.7/06.8 command architecture.

07.7.1Acute engagement (< 5 min)

Inside a five-minute window (ambush, close contact), 03.2 OODA dominates because the faster loop wins. 06.2 Relax-Look-Around-Make-a-Call compresses to exhale plus scan plus call. 03.5 Weakness-Biased Training pays out through dry-fire reps and stress drills producing the sub-five-second response. 00.8 mode reads Crisis. Subsystems requiring cognitive budget (06.4 deep intel analysis) go dark until exit.

07.7.2Short engagement (5–60 min)

From five to sixty minutes, 03.7 React-to-Contact runs sustained small-unit engagement. 06.7 Prioritize and Execute executes in full form. 03.8 Ambush and Defense decisions evaluate at fifteen-minute points. 06.6 ACE plus SITREP push at engagement breaks.

07.7.3Extended engagement (1–24 hr)

From one to twenty-four hours, 06.8 plans-briefs-debriefs compress. 06.7 Decentralized Command becomes essential because no single leader manages beyond six to ten continuously. 01.1 Rule of Threes respects (water, hypothermia). 01.7 Prolonged Field Care runs if casualty present. 02.10 Zone 2 caps sustained movement because higher intensity burns out inside sixty minutes.

07.7.4Extraction windows

< 30 min — MARCH/PAWS complete to stable9-line CASEVACminimal beyond life-preserving · PACE Primary
24–72 hr — Prolonged Field Care15-min re-MARCHhydration · pain ladder · SOAP every 30 min · multi-period thermal
NO EXTRACTION — 01 Primary self-sufficient04.B Self-Sufficient Pharmacy06.3 connect-or-isolate medical care · 06.7 leadership carries duration

With extraction available under thirty minutes, 01.6 MARCH/PAWS completes to stable. 06.6 9-line CASEVAC assembles. Intervention stays minimal beyond life-preserving. 06.6 PACE Primary holds.

At twenty-four to seventy-two hours, 01.7 Prolonged Field Care doctrine runs. 01.4 water treatment sustains. 01.2 casualty thermal protection holds across multiple periods. 06.4 situation report pattern runs to evacuation asset.

07.7.5Sustained horizons (1–7 d / 1–4 wk / > 1 mo / > 1 yr)

Inside one to seven days, 05.2 seven-day cache depth holds. 01.9 ten-Cs kit maps to Rule of Threes. 02.10 aerobic-base pacing (polarized eighty-twenty) preserves capacity. 06.6 PACE includes scheduled net-checks rather than continuous listening. 06.4 Daily Intelligence Check-Up holds at five to ten minutes routine.

At one to four weeks, 05.2 thirty-day stockpile holds. 05.3 food production overlays if seasonal window aligns. 02.10 training cycle shifts to maintenance at four to six hours per week minimum. 06.8 weekly tactical decision exercise enforces. 06.4 area study updates.

Beyond one month, 05.10 three horizons engage fully. 05.3 Restoration Agriculture architecture loads. 05.6 three energy chains rotate at full. 06.7 leadership cycle expands to monthly compound audit per 04.7. 06.8 weekly decisional cadence holds. 06.4 area study iterates through v2, v3.

Beyond one year (collapse or prolonged grid-down), 05.9 homestead architecture becomes the operating environment. 05.10 three horizons all run. 06.3 4GW grand strategy holds at household, community, and region scale. 05.7 tool production fills materiel gaps. 06.7 legitimacy discipline sustains.

07.7.6Cadence chains

Single events revert to baseline within twenty-four hours. 00.8 returns to Alert. 06.7 post-op debrief runs. 04.7 compound audit defers unless the event exposed weakness.

Episodic cadence (events every few days or weeks) engages 06.4 pattern-tracking in Area Study. 02.10 training cycle respects mission cadence. 04.7 quarterly compound review maintains.

Sustained cadence (daily engagement beyond seven days) makes 04.E physical specification substrate the ceiling. 06.7 Decentralized Command becomes essential. 06.7 rotation runs for any role with cognitive load. 00.7 Extreme Ownership forestalls excuse cascade.

Continuous cadence (active contact, pursuit, ongoing crisis) makes 00.9 at one hundred percent unsustainable. Rotation requires. 01.7 sleep-deficit signature watches through 00.7 PA flags. 04.7 compound drift begins at roughly two weeks disuse of any constituent domain.

07.7.7Habit formation stages

DEF

8 / 21 / 100 — 8-day conscious-effort drop · 21-day habit formed · 100-day automatic. Pleasant environments near 8-day end; high-stress environments closer to 21-day or longer.

In BASE training phase, 02.10 Zone 1 and Zone 2 polarized volume dominates at seventy to eighty-five percent of training volume. Combatives and alpine at maintenance (last session under fourteen days). 06.8 weekly tactical decision exercise runs.

In PEAK, 02.10 primary-domain emphasis loads. 04.7 compound FAILED risk rises if other domains drop below the thirty-day-touch floor. 00.7 PA halts further intensity on overtraining signatures.

In TAPER pre-objective, 02.10 tapering protocol runs. 04.7 pre-mission compound check executes. 06.8 final brief-to-lowest-common-denominator completes.

In RECOVERY (post-mission or post-injury), 02.10 gradualness rule caps at five to fifteen percent volume increase per week. 04.E floor maintains. 01.7 injury rehabilitation engages if applicable. 06.7 debrief runs as institutional learning.

07.7.8Time-to-dark chain

Inside ninety minutes to last light with position unsecured, 01.2 shelter executes at PRIORITY over 02-TRAVERSE. 01.3 fire preps in daylight. 00.9 cardinal-directions comms brief for night posture. 00.3 light discipline briefs.

Inside thirty minutes with shelter resolved but movement necessary, 00.3 NVG discipline (if equipped) loads. 02.2 compass bearing pre-sets. 02.8 night tracking runs if following sign. 06.6 comms schedule shifts to night-cadence with reduced ambient RF.

07.7.9Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the temporal chain through the Rule of Threes memorization, the compound-drift clock tracking across domains, and the time-to-dark calculation that fires ninety minutes before last light.

It functions when horizon band reads cleanly off calendar, when cadence elevates substrate preservation over tactical ambition on sustained engagement, and when compound drift is audited against the clock, not against comfort.

It fails when horizon is mis-read (treating a one-year problem as a one-week problem), when cadence ignores substrate collapse, or when habit-formation stages are rushed past the twenty-one-day mark.

Temporal feeds forward into 07.8 — command conditions modulate how temporal discipline scales across team.

SECTION 07.8

Command conditions — span, information environment, authority, civilians

Span ladder solo · buddy · fire team (4–5) · squad (8–13) · platoon (~16) · Information bands permissive · degraded · denied · hostile · Authority states clear-leader · clear-subordinate · disputed · collapsed · hostile · Civilian density zero · incidental · crowd · dominant · CP states established · mobile · degraded · none · Span max 6–10 direct, 4–5 preferred for combat elements

**S**pan-of-control chains scale from solo upward. Information-environment chains route by intel flow. Authority-chain chains route by legitimacy and position. Civilian-presence chains scale with 4GW weight. Command-post chains route by CP state.

This section installs the five-rung span ladder, the four-band information-environment calibration, the five authority-state chains, the four-density civilian-presence scaling against the 4GW weight function, and the four-state CP chain. Sources: 06.7 Willink laws, 06.8 team architecture, 06.3 4GW, 06.4 intelligence, 06.5 PSYOP, 06.6 comms, 00.4 Gray Man, 00.7 Personal Awareness.

07.8.1Span ladder — solo through platoon

SOLO — Extreme Ownership pure00.9 full cognitive load06.2 Detachment critical · 03.10 E&E default · PACE simplified
BUDDY — 03.7 Buddy-Pair Building Block03.6 Cover and Move06.7 Simple (either executes alone) · scheduled check-ins
FIRE TEAM (4–5) — 06.7 Decentralized Command at team-leaderCommander's Intent in ≤ 2 sentencesall Four Laws · Left-and-Right Limits briefed
SQUAD (8–13) — 06.8 squad architecturespan-of-control limit activesquad leader off the trigger · PACE multi-team · intel cell designated
PLATOON (~16) — 06.8 platoon architectureDecentralized Command mandatoryplans-briefs-debriefs formalized · leader at altitude

Solo operator loads 00.7 Extreme Ownership as pure self-accountability. 00.9 carries full cognitive load. 04.7 compound audit runs on self. 06.2 Detachment more critical because no team cues it. 03.10 E&E as default posture under adverse conditions. 06.6 PACE simplified to external contacts.

Fire team (four to five) runs 06.7 Decentralized Command at fire-team-leader level. 06.8 fire-team architecture (four to five shooters, designated leader). Commander's Intent in two sentences or fewer. All Four Laws of Combat in force. 06.8 Left-and-Right Limits briefed (what leader may decide alone, check, or never decide).

Platoon (~16) runs 06.8 platoon architecture (two squads plus HQ). 06.7 Decentralized Command mandatory. 06.8 plans-briefs-debriefs formalized. 06.8 "stand back and be the tactical genius" keeping leader at altitude.

07.8.2Information environment — four bands

Information-permissive (comms open, intel flowing) loads 06.4 Daily Intelligence Check-Up baseline. 06.6 PACE all channels up. 06.7 lead-down-the-chain telling operators why. 06.5 legitimacy acts visible.

Information-degraded (partial, intermittent, suspect) runs 06.6 PACE Alternate primary. 06.4 source evaluation strict under admiralty scale. 06.6 brevity plus pre-shared codes. 06.8 Commander's Intent carrying the gap when subordinates act without direction.

Information-denied (comms hostile, jammed, compromised) runs 06.6 Contingency or Emergency (physical runner, pre-arranged rendezvous). 06.4 pre-specified Indicators and Warnings substituting for live intel. 06.6 DF-mitigation. 06.4 compartmentation via cell architecture preserving information even under capture.

Hostile information environment (active PSYOP against operator, team, community) runs 06.5 counter-messaging via truth-first rule. 06.5 armed propaganda (every act visible, every act weighed against connect-or-isolate). 06.5 target-audience discrimination (primary, secondary, interior, exterior) before any response.

07.8.3Authority chain — five states

Clear chain with operator as leader loads Four Laws of Combat plus Extreme Ownership plus Dichotomy of Leadership fully. 06.8 architecture aligned to mission. 06.7 lead-up-the-chain discipline (push SA to higher).

Clear chain with operator as subordinate loads 06.7 lead-up-the-chain (push SA up). 06.7 play-the-game (build the relationship before spending capital). 06.7 check-the-ego. 06.7 Believe (ask up the chain until you understand the why).

Disputed authority (competing leaders, unclear lanes) runs 06.7 Prioritize and Execute naming the single highest priority and committing. 06.8 Left-and-Right Limits clarified in real-time. 06.7 ego check (mission success over personal prerogative). 06.2 Detachment restoring orientation before action.

Collapsed authority (no functioning chain, WROL) runs 03.9 Concentric Rings local defense. 06.3 4GW connection-and-isolation at whatever scale operator leads. 06.5 legitimacy built through visible competence and service. 06.7 "No bad teams, only bad leaders" holding the operator to step up or watch the team degrade.

Hostile authority override (authority figure is the adversary) runs 03.10 Absence primary. 00.4 Gray Man. 06.6 comms-compromised posture. 06.3 light-footprint-deep-root blending downward not upward. 04.C Information-Warfare OODA at full.

07.8.4Civilian-presence scaling

Zero civilians loads 06.3 Tactical-times-Physical dominant. Force response runs unconstrained beyond ROE. 03.8 ambush and 03.9 defense geometries have full terrain.

Few civilians (incidental, not dominant) raises the Tactical-times-Moral coefficient — the strategic-corporal effect where one tactical action produces strategic-moral consequence. 03.3 Miller-Kane respects civilian presence at each level. 06.5 every-act-is-propaganda governs.

Many civilians (crowd, neighborhood) makes 06.3 Strategic-times-Moral dominant. Force pushes to the lowest Miller-Kane rung that terminates threat. 06.5 de-escalation visibly runs. 00.4 Gray Man holds for low-signature movement. 06.4 area study demographics become the dominant variable.

Dominant civilian presence (operator among, not imposing upon) defaults to 06.3 De-escalation Model over Hama Model. 06.5 armed propaganda (repair a well, treat a wound) runs. 06.5 front organizations or three-person cells stand up if clandestine work is required. 06.8 dual-purpose architecture holds public face versus operational fact.

07.8.5Command post — four states

Established and secured CP loads 06.6 PACE through CP as hub. 06.8 plans-briefs-debriefs cadenced. 06.4 intelligence cell operational. 03.9 Dolio Concentric Rings protecting CP.

Mobile CP (leader moves with element) makes 06.7 Decentralized Command essential because the leader cannot process live. 06.6 minimal CP comms (over-the-shoulder, short bursts). 06.8 pre-briefed SOPs cover leader's tactical engagement windows.

Degraded CP (damaged, relocated, leader engaged as shooter) runs 06.7 "a decision executed is worth two decisions still being argued" on highest-priority. 06.8 next-senior assumes until restored. 06.6 PACE collapses to whatever is still up.

No CP (hasty operation, routine patrol) runs 06.8 Commander's Intent plus SOPs carrying the gap. 06.7 lead-up-the-chain on significant deviation. 06.6 scheduled check-ins substituting for continuous coordination.

07.8.6Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

WARN

The command chain FAILS when the leader blames subordinates (excuse cascade per 00.7), when plan complexity exceeds lowest-common-denominator comprehension (Simple violation), or when span exceeds 6–10 without sub-architecture (06.8 violation).

You install the command chain through Commander's Intent articulation in one-to-two sentences, Left-and-Right Limits briefed for every team member at mission start, and the blameless debrief as institutional-learning default.

It functions when trust built in peacetime spends correctly in wartime, when 4GW weighting places moral above mental above physical at the decisive altitude, and when u the leader stays at altitude where errors in the weeds are visible u.

It fails when blame flows down-chain, when complexity exceeds comprehension, or when span breaks the architecture.

Command feeds forward into 07.9 — compound conditions stack command with other classes and force simultaneous chain activation.

SECTION 07.9

Compound condition matrices — parallel chains, priority resolution, ledger

Compound entries 12 two-or-three-class stacks · Priority law life > limb > eyesight > mission > comfort (Miller-Kane) · connect-or-isolate (06.3 4GW) · Override hierarchy 01-PRIMARY > 02-TRAVERSE on environmental CRITICAL · 03-APPLIED FORCE > both on adversarial CRITICAL active · 04.D compound > raw force in multi-person engagement · Trade-off ledger thermal v concealment · comms v OPSEC · speed v signature · load v mobility · engagement v E&E · training cycle v demand · autonomy v coherence · legitimacy v immediate advantage

**C**ompound conditions stack two or more classes at once. The single-class chain above each class provides the components. The compound matrix resolves how they run simultaneously, which takes precedence, and what degrades to preserve the higher-priority activation. Twelve compound-stack entries load here. Each resolution ties to the Miller-Kane-referenced priority law at the physiological level and to the connect-or-isolate law at the 06.3 strategic level.

This section installs the twelve compound-entry matrices, the priority-resolution doctrine that resolves which subsystem commands under stacked CRITICAL, and the eight-variable trade-off ledger that names every compound decision's cost. Sources: the full 00-06 stack operating as a braided matrix plus the 04 compound structures (04.A through 04.E).

07.9.1Contact + cold + closing extraction window

Contact stacked with cold-weather stacked with a closing extraction window runs 03.6 IMT and 03.7 React-to-Contact at priority for engagement. 01.2 thermal regulation maintained at pause intervals with mittens off for shooting then back between under the three-layer discipline. 02.6 catching feature identified for break-contact route. 06.6 SALUTE plus ACE plus CASEVAC 9-line assembling in parallel.

Priority resolves 03-APPLIED FORCE above 01-PRIMARY above 02-TRAVERSE for the first fifteen minutes. On broken contact, priority inverts to 01-PRIMARY (shelter) above 02-TRAVERSE (fallback movement) above 03-APPLIED FORCE (residual defensive posture).

WARN

Abort rule: escalate to E&E-at-any-cost when wind chill reaches the ten-minute skin-freeze threshold and contact has not broken. The environment will kill faster than the adversary.

07.9.2Casualty + active contact + cold

Casualty stacked with active contact stacked with cold runs TCCC Phase 1 Care Under Fire — suppress the threat, apply CAT tourniquet high and tight, move casualty to cover. 03.6 RTR simultaneous to casualty move. 06.7 Prioritize and Execute calling the sequence ("Set security. CAT on. Move.").

Priority resolves suppress, tourniquet, extract to cover in that order within sixty seconds, then 01.6 MARCH full sequence in Tactical Field Care, with the hypothermia step critical given the cold modifier because trauma casualty loses heat three times normal.

07.9.3Extended duration + grid-down + supply drawdown

Extended duration stacked with grid-down stacked with supply drawdown engages 05.10 three horizons, 05.3 food production, 05.6 three energy chains rotating, 05.4 root cellar plus greenhouse at full duty, 06.3 4GW light-footprint-deep-root for external engagement, 06.4 Daily Intelligence Check-Up on battery-radio schedule, 06.7 Decentralized Command across household members each owning a subsystem.

Priority resolves water above shelter-thermal above food above security above external comms above everything else (Rule of Threes inverted per stockpile depth). The trade-off drops training cycle to maintenance floor (04.E held, not built), compresses 06.8 weekly decision exercise to daily huddle, and compresses 04.7 quarterly compound audit to monthly because conditions demand faster drift-detection.

07.9.4Pre-attack indicators + civilian-dense + ambiguous authority

Pre-attack indicators stacked with civilian-dense environment stacked with ambiguous authority runs 00.4 Total Awareness System at full (SA, PA, CA, 3PA, Threat Awareness). 03.1 Hierarchy of Response from lowest rung. 00.4 Gray Man posture. 06.3 Strategic-times-Moral weighting. 03.3 Miller-Kane pre-authorized only to Level 2-3. 06.5 every-act-is-propaganda discipline.

Priority resolves Absence above De-escalation above Force. The 03.1 law ("the best self-defense is not being there") governs. 03.10 Break-Line-of-Sight is preferred over 03.6 RTR in dense civilian area. Force escalates only when IMOP all four confirm.

07.9.5Surveillance + team + comms degraded

Surveillance detected stacked with team operating stacked with comms degraded runs the 04.C Information-Warfare OODA compound (comms, intel, strategy) engaged. 06.6 PACE shifting to Alternate and Contingency. DF-mitigation via brevity and mobility and frequency agility. 06.5 three-person cell architecture review if clandestine operations contemplate. 06.4 counter-intel assessment on what the surveillance suggests about adversary knowledge. 00.4 Gray Man on individual basis even within team. 06.7 Commander's Intent re-briefed for contingency execution on further comms drop.

Priority resolves 04.C above routine training. Intelligence value of the surveillance pattern itself exceeds the immediate counter-surveillance response. Escalation triggers to 03.10 E&E with Emergency PACE when surveillance converges into active pursuit or contact setup.

07.9.6Casualty + alpine terrain + no extraction

Casualty stacked with alpine terrain stacked with no extraction runs 01.6 MARCH/PAWS full. 01.7 Prolonged Field Care across multiple cycles. 02.9 rope team preserved if descent needed (crevasse-rescue configured). 01.2 casualty thermal protection at maximum (survival bag, casualty wrap, insulation on snow barrier). 02.10 altitude-illness monitoring for patient and team per FOTH Chapter 21. 06.6 PACE for SAR callout if possible. 06.7 leadership carrying the multi-day horizon.

Priority resolves life-saving intervention above environmental protection above navigation to lower ground above communication. The 01.7 H-step is non-negotiable in cold plus trauma under the lethal triad. Escalation triggers to shelter-in-place plus 01.9 signaling plus multi-day 01.7 Prolonged Field Care when descent becomes impossible and HAPE or HACE develops.

07.9.7Fatigue debt + sustained contact + leadership load

Fatigue debt stacked with sustained contact stacked with leadership load runs 02.10 AeT pacing (Zone 1/2 default). 06.7 Decentralized Command plus role rotation. 04.E substrate floor check through 02.10 nose-breathing diagnostic. 00.7 PA discipline auditing leader first. 06.7 Relax-Look-Around-Make-a-Call prescribed hourly regardless of tactical demand.

Priority resolves substrate preservation above tactical optimization. A fatigued team makes errors that cost more than slower pace costs. Mood disruption plus resting-HR rise plus 00.7 PA impairment across multiple team members signatures overtrain-class failure and forces pause even under pressure.

07.9.8Grid-down + hostile authority + long horizon

Grid-down stacked with hostile authority stacked with long horizon runs 05.10 three horizons full. 06.3 4GW grand strategy at community scale. 05.9 homestead architecture as operating environment. 05.7 tool production filling materiel gap. 06.5 three-person cell and front-organization architecture for clandestine work. 06.6 PACE collapsed to courier plus physical rendezvous. 06.7 legitimacy discipline continuous. 06.4 area study daily.

Priority resolves 06.3 grand strategy (connection or isolation) above every other decision. Individual training cadence becomes collective (homestead is the team). 04.7 compound audit adjusts to annual against the horizon. 06.5 armed propaganda replaces most external-facing tactical action.

07.9.9Supply exhausted + mass casualty + no extraction

Supply exhausted stacked with mass casualty stacked with no extraction runs 01.6 triage across all casualties. 01.7 Prolonged Field Care on the immediate. 04.B Self-Sufficient Pharmacy compound if household accessible. 01.8 improvised pharmacy through five herbal preparations plus pain-ladder herbal analogs. 06.7 leader carrying delegation plus rotation across responder roles. 06.6 SAR request via every available PACE step including physical dispatch.

Priority resolves triage categorization driving resource allocation — expectant casualties comfort without treatment under hard resource logic. 01.7 sanitation-equals-medicine in field conditions becomes critical.

07.9.10Active contact + leader wounded + team dispersed

Active contact stacked with leader wounded stacked with team dispersed runs 01.6 Care Under Fire on the leader by adjacent team member. 06.7 Decentralized Command proving itself with next-senior or pre-designated assuming. 03.6 RTR by unaffected members. 06.8 pre-briefed SOPs covering transition moments. 06.6 SITREP plus ACE plus CASEVAC 9-line in parallel. 00.9 situational picture re-aggregated at the new leader.

Priority resolves tactical suppression of threat above casualty treatment (Care Under Fire phase) above leadership transition above reconsolidation. The chain FAILS if no member can assume leadership. Prevention is upstream through 06.8 Left-and-Right Limits briefed for every member at mission start.

07.9.11Sign + weather closing + shelter unresolved

Sign observed stacked with weather closing stacked with shelter unresolved runs 01.2 shelter protocol at PRIORITY over 02-TRAVERSE. 00.1 Signcutting Line completing only to confirm direction (not to pursue). 04.2 Detection/Counter-Detection Loop active with shelter location chosen per 02.6 handrail and catching-feature logic to stay off the sign's line. 01.3 fire discipline (smokeless or deferred per curfew or banking) chosen against adversary signature. 00.9 continuous situational picture at fifty percent cadence during shelter build. 06.6 PACE if comms available.

Priority resolves shelter within ninety minutes above continued movement. Shelter location chooses per sign plus signature. Escalation triggers to fire-plus-concealment or abandons concealment for survival when weather forces fire under 01.1 "primitive that is ignored is the one that kills."

07.9.12Full-stack entry — all seven classes CRITICAL

The full-stack entry resolves all seven classes at CRITICAL simultaneously — grid collapse, hostile authority, civilian unrest, extended horizon. Every 04 compound engages (04.A Detection/Counter-Detection, 04.B Self-Sufficient Pharmacy, 04.C Information-Warfare OODA, 04.D Command Under Fire, 04.E Physical Specification substrate). 05.10 three-horizon sustainment is the operating doctrine. 06.3 4GW runs at household, community, region. 06.9 Blackout Warfare protocols baseline. 03.9 Concentric Rings hold the defended position. 00.6 Area Study updates daily.

Priority resolves 06.3 grand strategy at policy level, 01-PRIMARY at day-to-day, 03-APPLIED FORCE at contact level, 04.D compound above all when force is in play, 04.C running continuously, 06.7 leadership as integrating factor.

The trade-off runs every domain at maintenance floor — build and peak training suspend, aggressive exploration suspends, every action weighs in connect-or-isolate logic — and 02.10 "speed is safety" inverts to "speed is exposure."

07.9.13Priority-resolution summary

01-PRIMARY > 02-TRAVERSE on environmental CRITICAL (thermoregulation will kill faster than immobility)
03-APPLIED FORCE > 01-PRIMARY on adversarial CRITICAL active (adversary will kill faster than cold under fire)
03 > 01 in casualty + contact, then 01 under Care Under Fire doctrine
00.9 ≥ 50% against any chain (loss of picture is loss of orientation is loss of survival)
06.7 Prioritize and Execute > leader's direct action (leader at altitude catches errors in the weeds)
04.E substrate preservation > tactical optimization when degradation signatures present
04.B medical scope extends beyond extraction window when none available
06.3 grand strategy > tactical choice in 4GW environments (moral level decisive)

07.9.14The operator's trade-off ledger

The operator's ledger names every trade. Thermal against concealment — fire and insulation produce thermal and olfactory signature — traded always against time-to-frostbite. Comms against OPSEC — every transmission is DF-triangulable; brevity and mobility mitigate — traded always against coordination value. Speed against signature — faster movement increases sound, track depth, and fatigue — traded always against current 00.8 mode. Load against mobility — more supplies extend horizon but reduce movement — traded always against expected horizon. Engagement against E&E — force extends contact duration; E&E preserves for future — traded always against Miller-Kane proportionality and IMOP satisfaction. Training cycle against operational demand — peak produces maximum capability for narrow window; maintenance produces sustained readiness — traded always against calendar of mission demand. Individual autonomy against team coherence — Decentralized Command maximizes span; tight coordination reduces decision latency but caps team size — traded always against the 06.8 four-to-five ideal. Legitimacy against immediate advantage — moral level beats physical in 4GW; every tactical win can be a strategic loss — traded always through connect-or-isolate.

u The ledger is the payload. Every compound decision references it. u

07.9.15Install, function, failure mode, feed-forward

You install the compound matrix through the priority-resolution summary memorized to reflex, the trade-off ledger named out loud on every compound decision, and the twelve entries rehearsed quarterly under stress drill.

It functions when priority resolves cleanly under stacked CRITICAL, when the ledger produces named trades rather than felt compromises, and when escalation-and-abort rules fire on threshold.

It fails when compound decisions collapse to felt urgency, when priority resolves to operator preference, or when the ledger goes unnamed.

Compound feeds forward into 07.10 — the matrix extends into VOLUME_002 by adding new condition classes whose entry points are pre-routed here.

Close — from matrix to operator

You now hold the deployment layer. Seven first-order condition classes, one hundred thirteen declarative if/then chains running across perceptual, environmental, adversarial, resource, physiological, temporal, and command domains. Twelve compound-matrix entries stacking two or three classes at once, each with parallel activation chains, priority resolution, calibration trade-offs, and escalation or abort rules. A priority-resolution table and trade-off ledger that name the doctrine at work in every compound decision. Thirteen VOLUME_002 condition-class placeholders pre-routed to their matrix entry points. Three background loops — 00.9 Continuous Situational Picture, 00.8 OODA and Modes of Awareness, 04.E Physical Specification substrate — running always underneath.

The seven sub-modules before this built the subsystems. This sub-module installed the query layer over them. You read the ground through 00. You hold shelter, fire, water, and medicine through 01. You move through 02. You engage through 03. You compound through 04. You sustain through 05. You command through 06. You deploy through 07 by naming the condition, activating the chain, and calibrating against the trade-off ledger until the exit rule triggers. The matrix is doctrine the operator references at the moment the condition presents itself, the way a clinician references a protocol manual: one condition, one chain, one execution, with the continuous picture updating and the next chain queuing behind.

VOLUME_001 closes here. The 157-source corpus synthesized into eight sub-modules, seventy-plus integrated sections, one live operating system. The four named gaps sit as the seed for VOLUME_002, each with its condition class pre-tagged and its matrix entry point pre-routed. Every subsystem named by section tag. Every chain calibrated. Every trade-off explicit.

You land in a situation. You read what you are looking at. You name the condition. You activate the chain. You calibrate against the ledger. You terminate at the exit rule and re-query the matrix against the updated picture. The volume runs. The operator is the integrating factor, the substrate, the authority, and the continuously recalibrating query engine against a field that never stops generating new conditions.

u CONSTRUCT_APPLICATIONS :: VOLUME_001 is the system you now carry. u

Condition classes 7 first-order + 1 compound · Severity bands BASELINE · WARNING · CRITICAL · Background loops 00.9 Continuous Situational Picture (100% transit / 50% engagement) · 00.8 Modes of Awareness (Alert → Pre-crisis → Crisis) · 04.E Operator Physical Specification · Chain count 113 declarative if/then chains · Compound entries 12 two-or-three-class stacks · Priority law 01-PRIMARY beats 02-TRAVERSE on environmental CRITICAL; 03-APPLIED FORCE beats both on adversarial CRITICAL active · Exit rules resolution · degradation past threshold · scope exceeded · priority override · Extension 13 VOLUME_002 condition-class placeholders pre-routed

**You finish six sub-modules carrying a stack of installed subsystems. Sign reading, area study, primary survival, traverse, applied force, the compound interlocks, sustainment infrastructure, command discipline. Sub-module 07 is the query layer over that stack. A field condition presents itself. The matrix answers which subsystems fire, in what sequence, at what calibration, until what termination rule. This sub-module installs the condition taxonomy across seven first-order classes plus one compound class, the severity-band calibration across BASELINE/WARNING/CRITICAL, the termination-rule set (resolution, degradation, scope exceeded, priority override), the priority-resolution doctrine that resolves which subsystem commands the moment when classes stack, and the trade-off ledger the operator references on every compound decision. Sources: the complete 00-06 stack operating as a braided query surface, plus the 157-source corpus indexed into a live-running estimate.

00.0The matrix as state engine

The matrix is read as a lookup surface over a live running estimate. You enter through the perceptual or environmental class that is loudest. You classify the condition against the taxonomy. You activate the if/then chain as a declarative order to the named subsystem. You calibrate the chain against condition severity and operator/team state. You terminate on resolution, on degradation past threshold, on scope exceeded, or on override from a higher-priority class. Every activation updates 00.9 Continuous Situational Picture, which then re-queries the matrix against drift.

DEF

STATE ENGINE — a decision architecture in which entry, execution, and exit rules are explicit, chains update a continuously running picture rather than halting at a leaf, and the operator reads state transitions live rather than following a fixed decision tree.

Three background loops run always. 00.9 Continuous Situational Picture runs at one hundred percent cadence in transit and alert, fifty percent under active engagement, and returns to one hundred percent within ten minutes of resolution. 00.8 OODA and the Modes of Awareness cycle (Alert, Pre-crisis, Crisis) transition under chain activation; every chain respects current mode for execution tempo. 04.E Operator Physical Specification substrate — aerobic base, movement vocabulary, combatives power, alpine capacity — holds the body at the tempo the chain requires. A substrate that has collapsed below floor collapses chains at the physical level regardless of tactical clarity.

Sequence discipline is strict. Steps execute in the order named. Parallel steps are called out as "in parallel" or "simultaneous with." Priority override: 01-PRIMARY (shelter, fire, water, medical-immediate) beats 02-TRAVERSE whenever physiological or environmental class is CRITICAL, except when adversarial class is CRITICAL and contact is active, at which point 03-APPLIED FORCE (break contact or engage) beats both. Calibration is named in four bands — cadence (time units), intensity (percent of budget or baseline/elevated/maximum), intervention depth (hasty versus deliberate, break-contact versus engage), and degradation signature (the named marker that signals the chain is failing).

SECTIONS

A unified operating system for construct applications. 157 source texts synthesized into eight interlocking sub-modules: perception, survival primitives, movement, applied force, compound interlock, sustainment infrastructure, command, and systematic field deployment. Every section carries install protocols, calibration thresholds, and failure modes. The volume operates as a reference an operator reads in the field, not a book an operator reads at the fire.

ENTER VOLUME CATALOG
VOLUME ARCHITECTURE

THE RSI PROGRESSION

The volume follows the Recursive Self-Improvement progression from Extract_SYNTHESIS: baseline diagnostics, foundational architecture, acceleration protocols, optimization and stabilization, domain-specific deployment. Eight sub-modules map across the five RSI beats. The operator's arc reads: you assess, you survive, you move, you engage, you compound, you sustain, you command, you deploy.

00 GROUND LEVEL — BASELINE / DIAGNOSTICS → 01 PRIMARY SYSTEMS — FOUNDATIONAL ARCHITECTURE (1/3) → 02 TRAVERSE — FOUNDATIONAL ARCHITECTURE (2/3) → 03 APPLIED FORCE — FOUNDATIONAL ARCHITECTURE (3/3) → 04 THE COMPOUND — ACCELERATION PROTOCOLS → 05 SUSTAINMENT — OPTIMIZATION & STABILIZATION (1/2) → 06 COMMAND — OPTIMIZATION & STABILIZATION (2/2) → 07 FIELD DEPLOYMENT — DOMAIN-SPECIFIC DEPLOYMENT →
SYNTHESIS PRINCIPLES

THE METHODOLOGY

Five principles govern how the volume was built and how it should be read. They are the structural spine of every section, every interlock, every condition in the deployment matrix.

CROSS-SOURCE SYNTHESIS

Every section weaves insights from at least two source texts. When one framework clarifies another's technique, the clarification shows up in the prose. When two authors disagree, the disagreement resolves structurally or presents as a design choice.

OPERATIONAL HANDOFF

No insight without application. Every framework carries install steps, calibration thresholds, functioning indicators, and failure modes. If a concept cannot name its application, it does not appear in the volume.

COMPOUND-SYSTEM FRAMING

Individual techniques are scaffolding. The system is the asset. Every skill connects to adjacent skills through named feedback loops, and the compound architecture is the thing installed.

DEPTH OVER BREADTH

Each section stands alone as a comprehensive operational reference. A reader arriving at 03.6 without reading the rest gets the full mechanism, full application, full context. No highlight reel.

EVIDENCE AS PROSE

Technical and scientific content integrates into paragraphs as established knowledge. Specific numbers, measurements, and mechanisms named directly. Authority comes through specificity, not appeals to consensus.
